bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第133卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 133
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 133

sentences.zh: 【宋紀十五】 起重光大淵獻，盡旃蒙單閼，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 15] From guangda yuānxian through zhānméng shányán, altogether five years.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 15] Covering the five years from the guangda yuānxian cycle year through zhānméng shányán.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝下泰始七年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the annals of Emperor Ming Taizong, seventh year of Taishi (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Ming Taizong, seventh year of Taishi (

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元四七一年）

translations.literal: xīnhài, corresponding to the year 471 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xīnhài [sexagenary year], AD 471)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，戊戌，分交、廣置越州，治臨漳。

translations.literal: Spring, second month, on day wùxū, from Jiao and Guang [provinces] Yue Prefecture was established, with its seat at Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, on the day wūxū [16 February 471], Yue Prefecture was carved out of Jiao and Guang, with its capital at Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 初，上為諸王，寬和有令譽，獨為世祖所親。

translations.literal: Initially, when the emperor was among the princes, he was tolerant and harmonious and had a fine reputation; he alone was favored by Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while still a prince, the emperor was known for his clemency and amiability and enjoyed an excellent reputation; of all the princes, he alone was cherished by Emperor Shizu [Emperor Wen].

sentences.zh: 即位之初，義嘉之黨多蒙全宥，隨才引用，有如舊臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession, many of the Yijia faction received full pardon; according to their talents they were employed, as if they were old officials.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign, many members of the Yijia faction were spared and appointed according to their abilities, much like veteran ministers of old.

sentences.zh: 及晚年，更猜忌忍虐，好鬼神，多忌諱，言語、文書，有禍敗、凶喪及疑似之言應迴避者數百千品，有犯必加罪戮。

translations.literal: By his later years he became still more suspicious, cruel, and fond of spirits and omens, with many taboos: in speech and documents, calamity, defeat, mourning, and words of doubtful meaning to be avoided numbered in the hundreds and thousands of categories; whoever violated them was certainly punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew still more suspicious and cruel, obsessed with spirits and omens and burdened with taboos: speech and documents had to avoid hundreds and thousands of categories of words suggesting calamity, defeat, mourning, or anything remotely ominous—and any breach brought certain execution.

sentences.zh: 改「騧」字為「」，以其似禍字故也。

translations.literal: He even altered the written form of the character for "dapple-gray horse," because its shape too closely resembled the character for calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He even altered the written form of the character for "dapple-gray horse," because its shape too closely resembled the character for calamity.

sentences.zh: 左右忤意，往往有刳斫者。

translations.literal: Those at his side who displeased him were often disemboweled or hacked apart.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants who crossed him were often disemboweled or hacked to pieces.

sentences.zh: 時淮、泗用兵，府藏空竭，內外百官，並斷俸祿。

translations.literal: At the time warfare was being waged on the Huai and Si [rivers], the treasury was exhausted, and all civil and military officials alike had their salaries cut off.
translations.idiomatic: War on the Huai and Si fronts had drained the treasury, and salaries were suspended for officials throughout the government.

sentences.zh: 而上奢費過度，每所造器用，必為正御、副御、次副各三十枚。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's extravagance was excessive: for every utensil he had made, he ordered thirty each of the primary set, the secondary set, and the tertiary set.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor spent lavishly beyond measure: for every object he commissioned, he ordered thirty copies each for the primary, secondary, and tertiary imperial sets.

sentences.zh: 嬖倖用事，貨賂公行。

translations.literal: Favorites held power, and bribery was openly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Favored courtiers wielded power, and bribery was practiced openly.

sentences.zh: 上素無子，密取諸王姬有孕者內宮中，生男則殺其母，使寵姬子之。

translations.literal: The emperor had long been without a son; he secretly took into the palace pregnant consorts of the princes, and when a boy was born he killed the mother and had a favored consort raise the child as her own.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long been without an heir; he secretly brought pregnant consorts of the princes into the palace, and whenever a boy was born he had the mother killed and a favored consort raise the child as her own.

sentences.zh: 至是寢疾，以太子幼弱，深忌諸弟。

translations.literal: By this time he lay ill in bed; because the crown prince was young and weak, he deeply feared his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was bedridden with illness; with the crown prince still young and frail, he deeply distrusted his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史晉平刺王休祐，前鎮江陵，貪虐無度，上不使之鎮，留之建康，遣上佐行府州事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jinping, the Spiny King Xiuyou, governor of South Xuzhou, had previously been stationed at Jiangling and was greedy and cruel beyond measure; the emperor would not let him return to his post, kept him in Jiankang, and sent a senior aide to administer the prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuyou of Jinping, the Spiny King and governor of South Xuzhou, had earlier governed Jiangling with boundless greed and cruelty; the emperor refused to let him return to his post, kept him in Jiankang, and sent a senior aide to run the prefecture and province in his name.

sentences.zh: 休祐性剛很，前後忤上非一，上積不能平，且慮將來難制，欲方便除之。

translations.literal: Xiuyou's nature was stubborn and harsh; he had offended the emperor more than once, and the emperor's resentment had long gone unresolved; moreover he feared that in the future Xiuyou would be hard to control, and wished to remove him at a convenient opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou was stubborn and abrasive and had crossed the emperor repeatedly; resentment had festered for years, and the emperor also feared he would be hard to control later—so he looked for a chance to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，休祐從上於巖山射雉，左右從者並在仗後。

translations.literal: On day jiǎyín, Xiuyou accompanied the emperor to Yanshan to shoot pheasants; the attendants on left and right were all behind the armed guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiǎyín [11 March 471], Xiuyou accompanied the emperor to Yanshan for pheasant hunting; all the attendants were kept behind the armed escort.

sentences.zh: 日欲暗，上遣左右壽寂之等數人，逼休祐令墜馬，因共毆，拉殺之，傳呼「驃騎落馬！」

translations.literal: As the day was about to darken, the emperor sent several men of his entourage, including Shou Jizhi, to force Xiuyou to fall from his horse, then together they beat him and strangled him to death, crying out, "The Cavalry General has fallen from his horse!"
translations.idiomatic: As dusk approached, the emperor sent several attendants, including Shou Jizhi, to force Xiuyou from his horse; they then beat and strangled him to death while shouting, "The Cavalry General has fallen from his horse!"

sentences.zh: 上陽驚，遣御醫絡驛就視，比其左右至，休祐已絕。

translations.literal: The emperor feigned alarm and sent imperial physicians post-haste to examine him; by the time his attendants arrived, Xiuyou was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pretended to be alarmed and sent imperial physicians post-haste to attend him; by the time Xiuyou's own attendants arrived, he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 去車輪，輿還第。

translations.literal: The wheels were removed [from the carriage], and he was carried back to his residence in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: The wheels were removed from the carriage, and his body was carried back to his residence in a litter.

sentences.zh: 追贈司空，葬之如禮。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was enfeoffed as Minister of Works and buried with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and buried with full honors.

sentences.zh: 建康民間訛言，荊州刺史巴陵王休若有至貴之相，上以此言報之，休若憂懼。

translations.literal: Among the people of Jiankang a rumor spread that Prince Xiuruo of Baling, governor of Jingzhou, had the physiognomy of one destined for supreme honor; the emperor reported this rumor to him, and Xiuruo grew anxious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: A rumor spread through Jiankang that Prince Xiuruo of Baling, governor of Jingzhou, bore the countenance of a man destined for supreme power; the emperor relayed the rumor to him personally, and Xiuruo was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以休若代休祐為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On day wùwǔ, Xiuruo was appointed to replace Xiuyou as governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùwǔ [15 March 471], Xiuruo was appointed to replace Xiuyou as governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 休若腹心將佐，皆謂休若還朝，必不免禍。

translations.literal: Xiuruo's trusted generals and aides all said that if Xiuruo returned to court he would certainly not escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo's closest generals and staff all agreed that if he returned to court he would not escape death.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍京兆王敬先說休若曰：「今主上彌留，政成省閣，群豎恟□，欲悉去宗支以便其私。

translations.literal: Central Army Major Wang Jingxian of Jingzhao said to Xiuruo: "Now the emperor is on his deathbed; government is in the hands of the Secretariat, and the petty minions are in an uproar and terrified, wishing to remove all members of the imperial clan to serve their private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Major Wang Jingxian of Jingzhao urged Xiuruo: "The emperor is dying; power rests with the Secretariat, and the petty courtiers are panicking—they mean to purge every prince of the blood to serve their own ends.

sentences.zh: 殿下聲著海內，受詔入朝，必往而不返。

translations.literal: Your Highness's fame resounds throughout the realm; if you accept the summons to court, you will surely go but not return.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's renown fills the realm; if you obey a summons to court, you will go and never return.

sentences.zh: 荊州帶甲十餘萬，地方數千里，上可以匡天子，除奸臣，下可以保境土，全一身；

translations.literal: Jingzhou has more than a hundred thousand armored troops and a territory of several thousand li: on the one hand you can support the Son of Heaven and remove wicked ministers; on the other you can secure your borders and preserve your own person;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou fields more than a hundred thousand armed men across thousands of li of territory: you could restore the Son of Heaven and purge wicked ministers, or simply hold your borders and save yourself—

sentences.zh: 孰與賜劍邸第，使臣妾飲泣而不敢葬乎！」

translations.literal: which is better than being granted a sword in your mansion and having your wives and concubines weep in secret without daring to bury you properly!"
translations.idiomatic: which is better than receiving a sword in your own hall while your household weeps in secret, too afraid even to bury you properly?"

sentences.zh: 休若素謹畏，偽許之。

translations.literal: Xiuruo had always been cautious and timid; he pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuruo had always been cautious and timid; he pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 敬先出，使人執之，以白於上而誅之。

translations.literal: When Jingxian left, Xiuruo had men seize him, reported him to the emperor, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxian left, Xiuruo had him seized, reported him to the emperor, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉，魏假員外散騎常侍邢祐來聘。

translations.literal: Third month, day xīnyǒu: Xing You of Wei, acting Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day xīnyǒu [20 March 471], Xing You of Northern Wei, acting Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, arrived on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 魏主使殿中尚書胡莫寒簡西部敕勒為殿中武士。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Palace Secretary Hu Mohan to select men from the western Tiele tribes as palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei emperor sent Palace Secretary Hu Mohan to draft men from the western Tiele tribes as palace guards.

sentences.zh: 莫寒大納貨賂，眾怒，殺莫寒及高平假鎮將奚陵。

translations.literal: Mohan took bribes on a large scale; the people were enraged and killed Mohan and Xi Ling, acting garrison commander of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Mohan extorted bribes on a grand scale; the tribesmen rose in fury and killed both Mohan and Xi Ling, the acting garrison commander of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，諸部敕勒皆叛。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: all the Tiele tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, all the Tiele tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 魏主使汝陰王天賜將兵討之，以給事中羅雲為前鋒；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor sent Prince Tianci of Ruyin at the head of troops to suppress them, with Attendant-within-the-Palace Luo Yun as vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Prince Tianci of Ruyin with an army to suppress them, appointing Attendant-within-the-Palace Luo Yun as vanguard;

sentences.zh: 敕勒詐降，襲雲，殺之，天賜僅以身免。

translations.literal: the Tiele feigned surrender, attacked Yun, killed him, and Tianci barely escaped with his own life.
translations.idiomatic: the Tiele feigned surrender, ambushed Yun, and killed him; Tianci barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 晉平刺王既死，建安王休仁益不自安。

translations.literal: After the Spiny King of Jinping had died, Prince Xiuren of Jian'an grew still more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After the Spiny King of Jinping was dead, Prince Xiuren of Jian'an grew still more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 上與嬖臣楊運長等為身後之計，運長等慮上晏駕後，休仁秉政，己輩不得專權，彌贊成之。

translations.literal: The emperor and his favorite Yang Yunchang and others made plans for after his death; Yunchang and the rest feared that after the emperor's demise Xiuren would hold power and they themselves would be unable to monopolize authority, and they urged the matter on all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and his favorite Yang Yunchang and others plotted for the succession; Yunchang and his circle feared that once the emperor died Xiuren would seize power and they would lose their grip—and they pressed the emperor all the harder to act.

sentences.zh: 上疾嘗暴甚，內外莫不屬意於休仁，主書以下皆往東府訪休仁所親信，豫自結納；

translations.literal: The emperor's illness once grew suddenly severe; inside and outside the court all looked to Xiuren, and officials down to the clerks all went to the Eastern Palace to visit Xiuren's trusted men and establish ties in advance;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness once turned acute, everyone at court looked to Xiuren; even clerks visited his Eastern Palace faction to curry favor in advance;

sentences.zh: 其或在直不得出者，皆恐懼。

translations.literal: those who were on duty and could not leave were all fearful.
translations.idiomatic: those stuck on duty and unable to leave were terrified.

sentences.zh: 上聞，愈惡之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he hated Xiuren all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, his hatred for Xiuren deepened.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊午，召休仁入見，既而謂曰：「今夕停尚書下省宿，明可早來。」

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wùwǔ: Xiuren was summoned for an audience; afterward the emperor said to him, "Stay tonight at the lower offices of the Secretariat; come early tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wùwǔ [14 May 471], Xiuren was summoned to court; afterward the emperor told him, "Stay tonight in the lower offices of the Secretariat; come early tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 其夜，遣人繼藥賜死。

translations.literal: That night he sent men with successive doses of poison to grant him death.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent men with poison to grant him death.

sentences.zh: 休仁罵曰：「上得天下，誰之力邪！

translations.literal: Xiuren cursed, saying, "When Your Majesty won the realm, whose strength was it!
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren cursed him: "When you won the realm, whose strength was it!

sentences.zh: 孝武以誅金且兄弟，子孫滅絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu executed the Jin brothers, and his line was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu slaughtered the Jin brothers, and his line was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 今復為爾，宋祚其得久乎！」

translations.literal: Now you do the same again—how long can the Song mandate endure!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you do the same again—how long can the Song dynasty endure!"

sentences.zh: 上慮有變，力疾乘輿出端門，休仁死，乃入。

translations.literal: The emperor feared trouble, forced himself despite illness into his carriage and went out through the Duan Gate; only after Xiuren was dead did he return inside.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing an uprising, the emperor dragged himself from his sickbed into his carriage and rode out through the Duan Gate; only after Xiuren was dead did he return inside.

sentences.zh: 下詔稱：「休仁規結禁兵，謀為亂逆，朕未忍明法，申詔詰厲。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stating: "Xiuren plotted to win over the palace guard and intended rebellion; We could not bear to apply the law openly and sent repeated edicts to rebuke and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Xiuren plotted to suborn the palace guard and intended rebellion; We could not bear to punish him openly and sent repeated edicts to rebuke and question him.

sentences.zh: 休仁慚恩懼罪，遽自引決。

translations.literal: Xiuren, ashamed before Our grace and fearing punishment, hastily took his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren, ashamed before Our grace and fearing punishment, hastily took his own life.

sentences.zh: 可宥其二子，降為始安縣王，聽其子伯融襲封。」

translations.literal: His two sons may be spared; he is reduced to Prince of Shian County, and his son Borong is permitted to inherit the fief."
translations.idiomatic: His two sons are to be spared; his title is reduced to Prince of Shian County, and his son Borong is permitted to inherit the fief."

sentences.zh: 上慮人情不悅，乃與諸大臣及方鎮詔，稱：「休仁與休祐深相親結，語休祐云：『汝但作佞，此法自足安身；

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing that public sentiment would not be pleased, sent edicts to the great ministers and regional commanders saying: "Xiuren and Xiuyou were deeply bound in friendship; Xiuren told Xiuyou, 'You need only play the sycophant—this method alone is enough to keep yourself safe;
translations.idiomatic: Fearing public discontent, the emperor circulated edicts to senior ministers and regional commanders claiming: "Xiuren and Xiuyou were deeply allied; Xiuren told Xiuyou, 'You need only play the sycophant—that alone will keep you safe;

sentences.zh: 我從來頗得此力。』

translations.literal: I myself have always drawn considerable strength from this method.'
translations.idiomatic: I myself have always drawn considerable strength from that approach.'

sentences.zh: 休祐之隕，本欲為民除患，而休仁從此日生嬈懼。

translations.literal: Xiuyou's fall was originally meant to remove a scourge from the people, but from that day Xiuren grew daily more troubled and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou's death was meant to rid the people of a scourge, but from that day Xiuren grew daily more agitated and afraid.

sentences.zh: 吾每呼令入省，便入辭楊太妃。

translations.literal: Whenever I summoned him to the Secretariat, he would first go in to take leave of Empress Dowager Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I summoned him to the Secretariat, he would first go to bid farewell to Empress Dowager Yang.

sentences.zh: 吾春中多與之射雉，或陰雨不出，休仁輒語左右云：『我已復得今一日。』

translations.literal: In spring I often went pheasant hunting with him; when rain kept us from going out, Xiuren would tell those at his side, 'I have won another day.'
translations.idiomatic: In spring I often hunted pheasants with him; when rain kept us indoors, Xiuren would tell his attendants, 'I have won another day.'

sentences.zh: 休仁既經南討，與宿衛將帥經習狎共事。

translations.literal: Having campaigned in the south, Xiuren was long familiar and intimate with the commanders of the palace guard from working together.
translations.idiomatic: Having campaigned in the south, Xiuren was on familiar, intimate terms with the palace-guard commanders from long service together.

sentences.zh: 吾前者積日失適，休仁出入殿省，無不和顏，厚相撫勞。

translations.literal: When I was ill for many days recently, Xiuren came and went through the palace offices always with a pleasant face, lavishing comfort and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: During my recent long illness, Xiuren moved through the palace offices always wearing a pleasant face and lavishing comfort on everyone.

sentences.zh: 如其意趣，人莫能測。

translations.literal: As for his true intentions, no one could fathom them.
translations.idiomatic: His true intentions, no one could fathom.

sentences.zh: 事不獲已，反覆思惟，不得不有近日處分。

translations.literal: The matter could not be helped; after repeated reflection, recent measures could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The matter could not be helped; after long reflection, recent action became unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 恐當不必即解，故相報知。」

translations.literal: I fear you may not understand at once, and therefore inform you in advance."
translations.idiomatic: You may not grasp this at once, so I inform you in advance."

sentences.zh: 上與休仁素厚，雖殺之，每謂人曰：「我與建安年時相鄰，少便款狎。

translations.literal: The emperor and Xiuren had long been close; though he killed him, he often told others, "When I was young I lived next to Jian'an; from boyhood we were intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Xiuren had been close for years; though he had killed him, he often told others, "When we were young we lived side by side as neighbors; from boyhood we were intimate.

sentences.zh: 景和、泰始之間，勳誠實重；

translations.literal: Between the Jinghe and Taishi reigns his merit and loyalty were truly weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jinghe and Taishi reigns his merit and loyalty were truly great;

sentences.zh: 事計交切，不得不相除，痛念之至，不能自巳。」

translations.literal: affairs pressed urgently and we could not but remove one another—the grief when I think of it reaches the utmost; I cannot restrain myself."
translations.idiomatic: affairs pressed urgently and we could not but destroy one another—the grief when I think of it is unbearable; I cannot restrain myself."

sentences.zh: 因流涕不自勝。

translations.literal: And he would weep beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: And he would weep beyond control.

sentences.zh: 初，上在籓與褚淵以風素相善；

translations.literal: Initially, when the emperor was still a prince, he and Chu Yuan were on good terms for their shared refinement;
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while still a prince, he and Chu Yuan were close for their shared refinement of character;

sentences.zh: 及即位，深相委仗。

translations.literal: when he took the throne he entrusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: and when he took the throne he placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 上寢疾，淵為吳郡太守，急召之。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay ill, Yuan was governor of Wu Commandery and was urgently summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, Yuan was serving as governor of Wu Commandery and was urgently summoned.

sentences.zh: 既至，入見，上流涕曰：「吾近危篤，故召卿，欲使著黃衣羅耳。」

translations.literal: When he arrived and was received in audience, the emperor wept and said, "I have lately been gravely ill, and therefore summoned you—I wish to have you wear yellow gauze robes."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived and was received in audience, the emperor wept and said, "I have been gravely ill of late, and summoned you because I wish you to wear yellow gauze robes."

sentences.zh: 黃衣羅者，乳母服也。

translations.literal: Yellow gauze robes were the dress of a wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow gauze robes were the dress of a wet nurse.

sentences.zh: 上與淵謀誅建安王休仁，淵以為不可，上怒曰：「卿癡人！

translations.literal: The emperor plotted with Yuan to execute Prince Xiuren of Jian'an; Yuan thought it could not be done, and the emperor raged, saying, "You fool!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor plotted with Yuan to kill Prince Xiuren of Jian'an; Yuan objected, and the emperor raged: "You fool!

sentences.zh: 不足與計事！」

translations.literal: Not fit to plan affairs with!"
translations.idiomatic: Not fit to plan affairs with!"

sentences.zh: 淵懼而從命。

translations.literal: Yuan, in fear, obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, terrified, obeyed.

sentences.zh: 復以淵為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yuan was again appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was again appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以尚書右僕射袁粲為尚書令，褚淵為左僕射。

translations.literal: On day gēngwǔ, Yuan Can, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was made Director of the Secretariat, and Chu Yuan was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngwǔ [29 May 471], Yuan Can, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Secretariat, and Chu Yuan was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 上惡太子屯騎校尉壽寂之勇健；

translations.literal: The emperor hated Shou Jizhi, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry under the crown prince, for his courage and strength;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated Shou Jizhi, the crown prince's Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, for his courage and strength;

sentences.zh: 會有司奏寂之擅殺邏將，徙越州，於道殺之。

translations.literal: when the relevant office reported that Jizhi had killed a patrol commander without authority, he was banished to Yuezhou and killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: when the relevant office reported that Jizhi had killed a patrol commander without authority, he was banished to Yuezhou and killed en route.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，追廢晉平王休祐為庶人。

translations.literal: On day bǐngxū, Prince Xiuyou of Jinping was posthumously deposed and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bǐngxū [14 June 471], Prince Xiuyou of Jinping was posthumously deposed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若至京口，聞建安王死，益懼。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuruo of Baling reached Jingkou; when he heard that the Prince of Jian'an was dead, he grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuruo of Baling reached Jingkou; when he learned that the Prince of Jian'an was dead, his fear deepened.

sentences.zh: 上以休若和厚，能諧緝物情，恐將來傾奪幼主，欲遣使殺之，慮不奉詔；

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xiuruo was mild and generous and able to harmonize popular sentiment, feared that in the future he might overturn the young ruler; he wished to send men to kill him but feared they would not obey the order;
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiuruo was mild and popular and could win over hearts, the emperor feared he might one day displace the young heir; he wanted to send assassins but feared they would not obey;

sentences.zh: 欲征入朝，又恐猜駭。

translations.literal: he wished to summon him to court but again feared arousing suspicion and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: he considered summoning him to court but feared arousing suspicion and panic.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，以江州刺史桂陽王休范為南徐州刺史，以休若為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dīngyǒu: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang, governor of Jiangzhou, was made governor of South Xuzhou, and Xiuruo was made governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day dīngyǒu [25 June 471], Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was transferred from Jiangzhou to South Xuzhou, and Xiuruo was appointed governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 手書殷勤，召休若使赴七月七日宴。

translations.literal: In his own hand he wrote warmly, summoning Xiuruo to attend the feast on the seventh day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In his own hand he wrote warmly, summoning Xiuruo to attend the feast on the seventh day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主如河西。

translations.literal: On day dīngwèi, the Wei emperor went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dīngwèi [5 July 471], the Northern Wei emperor went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，巴陵哀王休若至建康；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the Lamented King Xiuruo of Baling reached Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Lamented King Xiuruo of Baling reached Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 乙丑，賜死於第，贈侍中、司空。

translations.literal: on day yǐchǒu he was granted death at his residence and posthumously given the titles of Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: on the day yǐchǒu [23 July 471] he was granted death at his residence and posthumously given the titles of Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 復以桂陽王休范為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was again made governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang was again appointed governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時上諸弟俱盡，唯休范以人才凡劣，不為上所忌，故得全。

translations.literal: By this time all the emperor's younger brothers were gone; only Xiufan, because his talent was mediocre and inferior, was not feared by the emperor, and therefore survived.
translations.idiomatic: By then all the emperor's younger brothers were dead; only Xiufan survived, because his abilities were mediocre and the emperor did not regard him as a threat.

sentences.zh: 沈約論曰：「聖人立法垂制，所以必稱先王，蓋由遺訓餘風，足以貽之來世也。

translations.literal: Shen Yue remarked: "When the sages established laws and handed down institutions, they always invoked the former kings—because the legacy of their teachings and the lingering force of their example are enough to bequeath to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue remarked: "When the sages established laws and handed down institutions, they always invoked the former kings—because the legacy of their teachings and the force of their example are enough to bequeath to later ages.

sentences.zh: 太祖經國之義雖弘，隆家之道不足。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Taizu's principles for ordering the state were broad, his way of exalting the clan was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Though Emperor Taizu's vision for governing the state was broad, his way of strengthening the imperial house was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 彭城王照不窺古，徒見昆弟之義，未識君臣之禮，冀以家情行之國道，主猜而猶犯，恩薄而未悟，致以呵訓之微行，遂成滅親之大禍。

translations.literal: Prince Yizhao of Pengcheng did not look into antiquity; he saw only the bond between brothers and did not understand the rites between ruler and subject. He hoped to apply family sentiment to the way of the state: the sovereign was suspicious yet he still transgressed; favor was thin yet he did not awaken—and a trifling act of rebuke and reproof led at last to the great calamity of destroying kin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yizhao of Pengcheng did not study antiquity; he saw only brotherly affection and failed to grasp the rites between ruler and subject. He hoped to govern the state by family sentiment: the sovereign grew suspicious yet he still overstepped; imperial favor waned yet he did not wake—and a minor act of rebuke and reproof led at last to the great catastrophe of destroying his own kin.

sentences.zh: 開端樹隙，垂之後人。

translations.literal: He opened the breach and planted the rift, and bequeathed it to those who came after.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the breach and planted the rift, and bequeathed it to posterity.

sentences.zh: 太宗因易隙之情，據已行之典，翦落洪枝，不得顧慮。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, taking advantage of the rift thus made easy, relied on precedent already set, and pruned away the great branches without regard for scruple.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, seizing on the rift thus opened, relied on precedent already established, and pruned away the great branches of the clan without scruple.

sentences.zh: 既而本根無庇，幼主孤立，神器以勢弱傾移，靈命隨樂推回改，斯蓋履霜有漸，堅冰自至，所由遠矣！」

translations.literal: Thereafter the root had no shelter, the young ruler stood alone, the sacred vessel shifted because power was weak, and the mandate turned with the tide of popular acclaim—this was surely frost underfoot growing by degrees until solid ice formed of itself; how far back the cause lay!"
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the dynastic root stood unprotected, the young ruler was isolated, the throne shifted as power weakened, and the mandate turned with the tide of acclaim—surely frost underfoot grows by degrees until solid ice forms of itself; how far back the cause reaches!"

sentences.zh: 裴子野論曰：「夫噬虎之獸，知愛己子；

translations.literal: Pei Ziye remarked: "Beasts that devour tigers know to love their own young;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye remarked: "Beasts that devour tigers still know to love their own young;

sentences.zh: 搏狸之鳥，非護異巢。

translations.literal: birds that strike wildcats do not protect nests not their own.
translations.idiomatic: birds that strike wildcats do not protect nests that are not their own.

sentences.zh: 太宗保字螟蛉，剿拉同氣，既迷在原之天屬，未識父子之自然。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong raised the name of the hornet's foster-child and slaughtered those of the same breath; he had lost sight of the heaven-ordained kinship expressed in the ode 'On the Highland,' and did not understand the natural bond between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong raised the name of the hornet's foster-child and slaughtered his own blood kin; he had forgotten the heaven-ordained bond of kin celebrated in the Odes, and failed to understand the natural tie between father and son.

sentences.zh: 宋德告終，非天廢也。

translations.literal: When the virtue of Song came to its end, it was not Heaven that cast it aside.
translations.idiomatic: When the virtue of Song came to its end, it was not Heaven that cast it aside.

sentences.zh: 夫危亡之君，未嘗不先棄本枝，嫗煦帝孽；

translations.literal: As for sovereigns on the brink of ruin, they never failed first to discard their root branches and cherish the emperor's collateral kin;
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns on the brink of ruin invariably discarded their root branches first and cherished the emperor's collateral kin;

sentences.zh: 推誠嬖狎，疾惡父兄。

translations.literal: they extended sincerity to favorites in intimacy and hated their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: they showed intimate trust to favorites and turned against their fathers and elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 前乘覆車，後來並轡。

translations.literal: Those who went before rode the overturned cart; those who came after drove abreast of them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who went before rode in the overturned cart; those who came after drove side by side with them.

sentences.zh: 借使叔仲有國，猶不先配天；

translations.literal: Even if Shuzhong possessed a state, he would still not be first to be mated with Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Even if Shuzhong had possessed a realm, he would still not have been first to match with Heaven;

sentences.zh: 而它人入室，將七廟絕祀；

translations.literal: yet others enter the house, and soon the sacrifices at the seven temples are cut off;
translations.idiomatic: yet others enter the house, and soon the sacrifices at the seven temples cease;

sentences.zh: 曾是莫懷，甘心手前落。

translations.literal: they never once awakened to this; they were willing to fall by their own hand.
translations.idiomatic: they never woke to this; they were content to fall by their own hand.

sentences.zh: 晉武背文明之托，而覆中州者賈後；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin betrayed the charge of Emperor Wenming, and the one who overthrew the Central Plains was Empress Jia;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin betrayed Emperor Wenming's charge, and the Central Plains were overthrown by Empress Jia;

sentences.zh: 太祖棄初寧之誓，而登合殿者元兇。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu abandoned the oath of Chuning, and the one who ascended the Hall of Union was the chief culprit;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu abandoned the oath of Chuning, and the one who ascended the Hall of Union was the chief culprit;

sentences.zh: 禍福無門，奚其豫擇！

translations.literal: Fortune and disaster have no fixed gate—why choose in advance!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune and disaster have no fixed gate—why choose in advance!

sentences.zh: 友于兄弟，不亦安乎！」

translations.literal: Be friendly to your brothers—is it not peace indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Be friendly to your brothers—is that not peace indeed!"

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏主至陰山。

translations.literal: On day bǐngyín the Wei emperor reached Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bǐngyín [27 July 471], the Northern Wei emperor reached Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 初，吳喜之討會稽也，言於上曰：「得尋陽王子房及諸賊帥，皆即於東戮之。」

translations.literal: Initially, when Wu Xi was campaigning against Kuaiji, he said to the emperor, "When we capture Zifang of Xunyang and the other rebel leaders, execute them all at once in the east."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi was campaigning against Kuaiji, he told the emperor, "When we capture Zifang of Xunyang and the other rebel leaders, execute them all at once in the east."

sentences.zh: 既而生送子房，釋顧琛等。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he sent Zifang alive and released Gu Chen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward he sent Zifang alive and released Gu Chen and others.

sentences.zh: 上以其新立大功，不問，而心銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xi had just achieved a great merit, did not pursue the matter, but bore a grudge in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Xi had just won a great victory, did not pursue the matter, but bore a grudge in his heart.

sentences.zh: 及克荊州，剽掠，贓以萬計。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was taken, he plundered, and booty was reckoned in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou was taken, he plundered on a vast scale, booty reckoned in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 壽寂之死，喜為淮陵太守，督豫州諸軍事，聞之，內懼，啟乞中散大夫，上猶疑駭。

translations.literal: When Shou Jizhi died, Xi was governor of Huailing and supervised military affairs in Yuzhou; hearing of it, he was inwardly afraid and petitioned to be made Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; the emperor still suspected and was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou Jizhi was killed, Xi was governor of Huailing supervising Yuzhou military affairs; hearing of it, he was inwardly terrified and petitioned for the post of Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; the emperor remained suspicious and alarmed.

sentences.zh: 或譖蕭道成在淮陰有貳心於魏，上封銀壺酒，使喜自持賜道成。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Xiao Daocheng at Huaiyin as having a divided heart toward Wei; the emperor sealed wine in a silver flask and had Xi carry it himself to present to Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Xiao Daocheng at Huaiyin as disloyal to Wei; the emperor sealed wine in a silver flask and had Xi carry it personally to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成懼，欲逃，喜以情告道成，且先為之飲，道成即飲之。

translations.literal: Daocheng was afraid and wished to flee; Xi told him the truth and first drank some for him; Daocheng then drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was afraid and wanted to flee; Xi told him the truth and drank first to prove it safe; Daocheng then drank.

sentences.zh: 喜還朝，保證道成。

translations.literal: Xi returned to court and vouched for Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi returned to court and vouched for Daocheng's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 或密以啟上，上以喜多計數，素得人情，恐其不能事幼主；

translations.literal: Someone secretly reported this to the emperor; the emperor, because Xi was full of schemes and had long won popular favor, feared he could not serve a young ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Someone secretly reported this to the emperor; because Xi was full of schemes and had long won popular favor, the emperor feared he would not serve a young ruler faithfully;

sentences.zh: 乃召喜入內殿，與共言謔甚款。

translations.literal: he therefore summoned Xi into the inner palace and jested with him very warmly.
translations.idiomatic: he summoned Xi into the inner palace and jested with him very warmly.

sentences.zh: 既出，賜以名饌。

translations.literal: When he came out, he was granted famous delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi left, the emperor granted him a feast of famous delicacies.

sentences.zh: 尋賜死，然猶發詔賻賜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted death, yet an edict was still issued for funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was put to death, yet an edict was still issued for funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 又與劉勉等詔曰：「吳喜輕狡萬端，苟取物情。

translations.literal: He also sent edicts to Liu Mian and others saying, "Wu Xi is frivolous and cunning in ten thousand ways, grasping at popular favor.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent edicts to Liu Mian and others saying, "Wu Xi is frivolous and cunning in countless ways, grasping at popular favor.

sentences.zh: 昔大明中，黟、歙有亡命數千人，攻縣邑，殺官長，劉子尚遣三千精甲討之，再往失利。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, in Yi and She several thousand outlaws attacked counties and towns and killed officials; Liu Zishang sent three thousand elite troops to suppress them and failed twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era, several thousand outlaws in Yi and She attacked counties and killed officials; Liu Zishang sent three thousand elite troops against them and failed twice.

sentences.zh: 孝武以喜將數十人至縣，說誘群賊，賊即歸降。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu sent Xi with several dozen men to the county; he persuaded and enticed the band of rebels, and they at once surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu sent Xi with several dozen men to the county; he persuaded the rebels, and they surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 詭數幻惑，乃能如此。

translations.literal: By deceitful schemes and illusory enticements he could accomplish such things.
translations.idiomatic: By deceitful schemes and illusory persuasion he could accomplish such things.

sentences.zh: 及泰始初東討，止有三百人，直造三吳，凡再經薄戰，而自破岡以東至海十郡，無不清蕩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi eastern campaign he had only three hundred men, marched straight into the Three Wu, fought only two light engagements in all, and from Pogang east to the sea ten commanderies were entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taishi eastern campaign he had only three hundred men, marched straight into the Three Wu, fought only two light engagements, and cleared ten commanderies from Pogang east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 百姓聞吳河東來，便望風自退；

translations.literal: when the people heard that Wu was coming from east of the river, they fled at the mere rumor;
translations.idiomatic: When the people heard that Wu was coming from east of the river, they fled at the mere rumor;

sentences.zh: 若非積取三吳人情，何以得弭伏如此！

translations.literal: if he had not long accumulated the goodwill of the Three Wu, how could he have pacified and subdued them so!
translations.idiomatic: without long accumulating goodwill in the Three Wu, how could he have pacified them so completely!

sentences.zh: 尋喜心跡，豈可奉守文之主，遭國家可乘之會邪！

translations.literal: Considering Xi's true intentions, how could he serve a ruler who upholds the written law when the state offers an opportunity to be seized!
translations.idiomatic: Given Xi's true intentions, how could he faithfully serve a young ruler when the state offered an opportunity to be seized!

sentences.zh: 譬如餌藥，當人羸冷，資散石以全身，及熱勢發動，去堅積以止患，非忘其功，勢不獲已耳。」

translations.literal: It is like taking medicine: when a man is weak and cold, powdered stone is used to preserve the body; when fever rises, harsh purgatives are removed to stop the illness—not forgetting his merit, but the situation leaves no choice."
translations.idiomatic: It is like medicine: when a man is weak and cold, a mild powder preserves him; when fever rises, harsh drugs are withdrawn—not forgetting his merit, but circumstances leave no choice."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以淮陰為北兗州，征蕭道成入朝。

translations.literal: On day wùyín, Huaiyin was made North Yanzhou, and Xiao Daocheng was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùyín [8 August 471], Huaiyin was made North Yanzhou, and Xiao Daocheng was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 道成所親以朝廷方誅大臣，勸勿就征，道成曰：「諸卿殊不見事！

translations.literal: Daocheng's intimates, because the court was then executing great ministers, urged him not to answer the summons; Daocheng said, "You gentlemen truly do not see how things stand!
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng's intimates, seeing the court executing great ministers, urged him not to go; Daocheng said, "You gentlemen truly do not understand!

sentences.zh: 主上自以太子稚弱，翦除諸弟，何預它人！

translations.literal: The sovereign himself, because the crown prince is young and weak, is cutting down his younger brothers—what has that to do with anyone else!
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign himself, because the crown prince is young, is cutting down his brothers—what has that to do with anyone else!

sentences.zh: 今唯應速發；

translations.literal: Now we should set out at once;
translations.idiomatic: We should set out at once;

sentences.zh: 淹留顧望，必將見疑。

translations.literal: if we linger and look back, we will surely be suspected.
translations.idiomatic: if we linger and hesitate, we will surely be suspected.

sentences.zh: 且骨肉相殘，自非靈長之祚，禍難將興，方與卿等戮力耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover, when flesh and blood destroy one another, it is not the fortune of a long-lived house; calamity is about to arise—we must strive together with you all."
translations.idiomatic: When kin slaughter kin, it is not the fortune of a long-lived dynasty; calamity is coming—we must strive together."

sentences.zh: 既至，拜散騎常侍、太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁亥，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day dīnghài: the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day dīnghài [27 August 471], the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以皇子躋繼江夏文獻王義恭。

translations.literal: On day wùzǐ, Prince Ji was made to succeed Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, the Cultivated King.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùzǐ [28 August 471], Prince Ji was made to succeed Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, the Cultivated King.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，上疾有間，大赦。

translations.literal: On day gēngyín the emperor's illness eased somewhat and a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngyín [30 August 471] the emperor's illness eased somewhat and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，立皇子淮為安成王，實桂陽王休范之子也。

translations.literal: On day wùxū Prince Huai was established as Prince of Ancheng—in fact he was the son of Prince Xiufan of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùxū [5 September 471] Prince Huai was established as Prince of Ancheng—in fact he was the son of Prince Xiufan of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 魏顯祖聰睿夙成，剛毅有斷，而好黃、老、浮屠之學。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu of Wei was clever and perceptive from youth, resolute and decisive, yet fond of the learning of Huang-Lao and Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu of Northern Wei was clever and perceptive from youth, resolute and decisive, yet fond of Huang-Lao and Buddhist learning.

sentences.zh: 每引朝士及沙門共談玄理，雅薄富貴，常有遺世之心。

translations.literal: He often summoned courtiers and monks to discuss arcane principles together; he naturally despised wealth and rank and often had a mind to leave the world.
translations.idiomatic: He often summoned courtiers and monks to discuss arcane principles; he naturally despised wealth and rank and often wished to renounce the world.

sentences.zh: 以叔父中都大官京兆王子推沉雅仁厚，素有時譽，欲禪以帝位。

translations.literal: Because his uncle, the Grand Palace Official of the Center, Prince Zitui of Jingzhao, was grave, elegant, benevolent, and generous and had long enjoyed a fine reputation, he wished to abdicate the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because his uncle Prince Zitui of Jingzhao, Grand Palace Official of the Center, was grave, elegant, and benevolent and had long enjoyed a fine reputation, he wished to abdicate in his favor.

sentences.zh: 時太尉源賀督諸軍屯漠南，馳傳召之。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Commandant Yuan He was supervising armies stationed south of the desert; he was summoned by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan He was then supervising armies south of the desert and was summoned by urgent relay.

sentences.zh: 既至，會公卿大議，皆莫敢先言。

translations.literal: When he arrived, a great council of dukes and ministers was convened; none dared speak first.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, a great council of dukes and ministers was convened; none dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 任城王雲，子推之弟也，對曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。

translations.literal: Prince Yun of Rencheng, Zitui's younger brother, replied: "Your Majesty is just now raising great peace and overseeing all within the four seas—how can you go against the ancestral temple above and abandon the myriad people below.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yun of Rencheng, Zitui's younger brother, replied: "Your Majesty is just now establishing great peace and ruling all within the four seas—how can you go against the ancestral temple above and abandon the myriad people below?

sentences.zh: 且父子相傳，其來久矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, transmission from father to son has been the practice for long ages.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, transmission from father to son has been the practice for ages.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲委棄塵務，則皇太子宜承正統。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must cast off worldly affairs, then the crown prince should inherit the legitimate succession.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must renounce worldly affairs, the crown prince should inherit the legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，祖宗之天下。

translations.literal: The realm belongs to the ancestors' realm.
translations.idiomatic: The realm belongs to the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 陛下若更授旁支，恐非先聖之意。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty transfers it to a collateral branch, I fear that is not the intent of the former sages.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty transfers it to a collateral branch, I fear that is not what the former sages intended.

sentences.zh: 啟奸亂之心，斯乃禍福之原，不可不懼也。」

translations.literal: It would awaken the heart of treachery and disorder—this is the source of fortune and disaster; it must be feared."
translations.idiomatic: It would awaken treachery and disorder—the source of fortune and disaster; it must be feared."

sentences.zh: 源賀曰：「陛下今欲禪位皇叔，臣恐紊亂昭穆，後世必有逆祀之譏。

translations.literal: Yuan He said: "Your Majesty now wishes to abdicate to the imperial uncle; I fear disorder in the order of zhao and mu, and later ages will surely reproach this as irregular sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He said: "Your Majesty now wishes to abdicate to your uncle; I fear disorder in the ancestral order, and later ages will surely reproach this as irregular sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 願深思任城之言。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to ponder deeply the words of the Prince of Rencheng."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ponder deeply the Prince of Rencheng's words."

sentences.zh: 東陽公丕等曰：「皇太子雖聖德早彰，然實沖幼。

translations.literal: Duke Pi of Dongyang and others said: "Though the crown prince's sage virtue has shown early, he is in truth still very young.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Pi of Dongyang and others said: "Though the crown prince's virtue has shown early, he is still very young.

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽萬機，奈何欲隆獨善，不以天下為心，其若宗廟何！

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has only begun to oversee the myriad affairs—why wish to exalt solitary goodness and not take the realm to heart? What of the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and has only begun to govern—why seek solitary withdrawal and not take the realm to heart? What of the ancestral temple!

sentences.zh: 其若億兆何！」

translations.literal: What of the hundred millions!"
translations.idiomatic: What of the hundred millions of people!"

sentences.zh: 尚書陸□曰：「陛下若捨皇太子，更方諸王，臣請刎頸殿庭，不敢奉詔！」

translations.literal: Minister Lu [Kai] said: "If Your Majesty abandons the crown prince and turns to another prince, I beg to cut my throat in the palace hall—I dare not obey such an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Kai said: "If Your Majesty abandons the crown prince for another prince, I beg to cut my throat in the palace hall—I dare not obey such an edict!"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，變色；

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and changed color;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry and changed color;

sentences.zh: 以問宦者選部尚書酒泉趙黑，黑曰：「臣以死奉戴皇太子，不知其它！」

translations.literal: he asked the eunuch, Minister of the Selection Bureau Zhao Hei of Jiuquan; Hei said, "I will die upholding the crown prince—I know nothing else!"
translations.idiomatic: he asked the eunuch, Minister of the Selection Bureau Zhao Hei of Jiuquan; Hei said, "I will die upholding the crown prince—I know nothing else!"

sentences.zh: 帝默然，時太子宏生五年矣，帝以其幼，故欲傳位子推。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent. At the time Crown Prince Hong was five years old; because he was young, the emperor therefore wished to pass the throne to Zitui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent. Crown Prince Hong was then five years old; because he was so young, the emperor had wished to pass the throne to Zitui.

sentences.zh: 中書令高允曰：「臣不敢多言，願陛下上思宗廟托付之重，追念周公抱成王之事。」

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun said, "I dare not say much; I wish Your Majesty would think above of the heavy charge of the ancestral temple and recall how the Duke of Zhou held King Cheng in his arms."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Gao Yun said, "I dare not say much; I wish Your Majesty would reflect on the heavy charge of the ancestral temple and recall how the Duke of Zhou held the infant King Cheng."

sentences.zh: 帝乃曰：「然則立太子，郡公輔之，有何不可！」

translations.literal: The emperor then said, "Then establish the crown prince and let the princes and dukes assist him—what is impossible in that!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then said, "Then establish the crown prince and let the princes assist him—what is wrong with that!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陸□，直臣也，必能保吾子。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Lu [Kai] is a straight minister; he will surely be able to protect my son."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Lu Kai is a straight minister; he will surely protect my son."

sentences.zh: 乃以□為太保，與源賀持節奉皇帝璽紱傳位於太子。

translations.literal: Thereupon [Lu Kai] was made Grand Tutor, and with Yuan He bearing the staff of authority they presented the imperial seal and cord and transferred the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Lu Kai was made Grand Tutor, and with Yuan He bearing the staff of authority they presented the imperial seal and cord and transferred the throne to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丙午，高祖即皇帝位，大赦，改元延興。

translations.literal: On day bǐngwǔ, Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yanxing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bǐngwǔ [9 September 471], Emperor Gaozu ascended the throne, declared a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yanxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖幼有至性，前年，顯祖病癰，高祖新吮。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu from youth had utmost filial nature; the year before, when Emperor Xianzu had an abscess, Gaozu sucked it fresh.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had been deeply filial from youth; the year before, when Emperor Xianzu had an abscess, Gaozu sucked it fresh himself.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，悲泣不自勝。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he wept in grief beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the abdication, he wept uncontrollably in grief.

sentences.zh: 顯祖問其故，對曰：「代親之感，內切於心。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu asked the reason; he replied, "The feeling of acting in a parent's place cuts deep within the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu asked why; he replied, "The feeling of standing in a parent's place cuts deep within the heart."

sentences.zh: 丁未，顯祖下詔曰：「朕希心玄古，志存淡泊，爰命儲宮踐升大位，朕得優遊恭己，棲心浩然。」

translations.literal: On day dīngwèi Emperor Xianzu issued an edict saying, "We set Our heart on the profound antiquity and keep Our will in simplicity; We have ordered the heir to ascend the great throne, that We may roam at ease in respectful retirement and lodge Our mind in vast calm."
translations.idiomatic: On the day dīngwèi [10 September 471] Emperor Xianzu issued an edict: "We set Our heart on profound antiquity and keep Our will in simplicity; We have ordered the heir to ascend the throne, that We may retire at ease and lodge Our mind in vast calm."

sentences.zh: 群臣奏曰：「昔漢高祖稱皇帝，尊其父為太上皇，明不統天下也。

translations.literal: The ministers memorialized, saying, "Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han assumed the title of emperor and honored his father as Supreme Emperor—making clear that he did not rule the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers memorialized: "Formerly Emperor Gaozu of Han took the throne and honored his father as Supreme Emperor—making clear that the father did not rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝幼沖，萬機大政，猶宜陛下總之。

translations.literal: Now the emperor is young and tender; the great affairs of the myriad duties should still be overseen by Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor is young; the great affairs of state should still be overseen by Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 謹上尊號曰太上皇帝。」

translations.literal: We respectfully offer the honorific title Supreme Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: We respectfully offer the honorific title Supreme Emperor."

sentences.zh: 顯祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu assented.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上皇徙居崇光宮，采椽不斫，土階而已；

translations.literal: On day jǐyǒu the Supreme Emperor moved to Chongguang Palace; rafters were left unplaned and there were only earthen steps;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐyǒu [12 September 471] the Supreme Emperor moved to Chongguang Palace; rafters were left unplaned and there were only earthen steps;

sentences.zh: 國之大事鹹以聞。

translations.literal: all great affairs of state were reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: all great affairs of state were still reported to him.

sentences.zh: 崇光宮在北苑中，又建鹿野浮圖於苑中之西山，與禪僧居之。

translations.literal: Chongguang Palace was in the Northern Park; he also built the Luye pagoda on the western hill within the park and dwelt there with Chan monks.
translations.idiomatic: Chongguang Palace stood in the Northern Park; he also built the Luye pagoda on the western hill within the park and lived there with Chan monks.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏沃野、統萬二鎮敕勒叛，遣太尉源賀帥眾討之；

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the Tiele of the Wo Ye and Tongwan garrisons rebelled; Grand Commandant Yuan He was sent at the head of troops to suppress them;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Tiele of the Wo Ye and Tongwan garrisons rebelled; Grand Commandant Yuan He was sent with an army to suppress them;

sentences.zh: 降二千餘落，追擊餘黨至枹罕、金城，大破之，斬首八千餘級，虜男女萬餘口，雜畜三萬餘頭。

translations.literal: more than two thousand clans surrendered; pursuing the remnant bandits to Baohan and Jincheng, he inflicted a great defeat, took more than eight thousand heads, captured men and women numbering more than ten thousand, and miscellaneous livestock more than thirty thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: more than two thousand clans surrendered; pursuing the remnant rebels to Baohan and Jincheng, he won a great victory, took more than eight thousand heads, captured more than ten thousand men and women, and more than thirty thousand head of livestock.

sentences.zh: 詔賀都督三道諸軍，屯於漠南。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command all armies of the three routes and encamp south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to command all armies of the three routes and encamp south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏每歲秋、冬發軍，三道並出，以備柔然，春中乃還。

translations.literal: Previously, Wei each year in autumn and winter sent out troops; the three routes marched out together to guard against the Rouran and returned only in mid-spring.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, each autumn and winter Wei sent troops out on three routes together to guard against the Rouran and did not return until mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 賀以為：「往來疲勞，不可支久；

translations.literal: He believed: "The to-and-fro weariness cannot be sustained for long;
translations.idiomatic: He argued: "The constant marching back and forth cannot be sustained;

sentences.zh: 請募諸州鎮武健者三萬餘人，築三城以處之，使冬則講武，春則耕種。」

translations.literal: I request recruiting more than thirty thousand stalwart men from the provinces and garrisons, building three cities to house them, so that in winter they drill in arms and in spring they farm."
translations.idiomatic: I request recruiting more than thirty thousand stalwart men from the provinces and garrisons, building three cities to house them, drilling in winter and farming in spring."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: His proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，魏以南安王楨為都督涼州及西戎諸軍事，領護西域校尉，鎮涼州。

translations.literal: On day gēngyín Prince Zhen of Nan'an was made commander of Liangzhou and all western Rong military affairs, Protector of the Western Regions Commandant, and stationed at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngyín [5 October 471] Prince Zhen of Nan'an was made commander of Liangzhou and all western Rong military affairs, Protector of the Western Regions, and stationed at Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命北琅邪、蘭陵二郡太守垣崇祖經略淮北，崇祖自郁洲將數百人入魏境七百里，據蒙山。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yuan Chongzu, governor of North Langye and Lanling commanderies, to operate north of the Huai; Chongzu led several hundred men from Yuzhou seven hundred li into Wei territory and seized Mengshan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yuan Chongzu, governor of North Langye and Lanling, to operate north of the Huai; Chongzu led several hundred men from Yuzhou seven hundred li into Wei territory and seized Mengshan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，魏東兗州刺史於洛侯擊之，崇祖引還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Yu Luohou, governor of East Yanzhou in Wei, attacked him, and Chongzu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yu Luohou, governor of East Yanzhou in Wei, attacked him, and Chongzu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上以故第為湘宮寺，備極壯麗；

translations.literal: The emperor made his former residence into Xiang Palace Temple, equipped with utmost splendor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor converted his former residence into Xiang Palace Temple, equipping it with utmost splendor;

sentences.zh: 欲造十級浮圖而不能，乃分為二。

translations.literal: he wished to build a ten-story pagoda but could not, and so divided it into two.
translations.idiomatic: he wished to build a ten-story pagoda but could not, and so built two instead.

sentences.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡入見，上謂曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi, governor of Xin'an, left his commandery and came for an audience; the emperor said to him, "Have you been to Xiang Palace Temple?
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi, governor of Xin'an, left his post and came for an audience; the emperor asked, "Have you been to Xiang Palace Temple?

sentences.zh: 此是我大功德，用錢不少。」

translations.literal: This is my great merit; the money spent was no small amount."
translations.idiomatic: This is my great merit; it cost no small sum."

sentences.zh: 通直散騎侍郎會稽虞願侍側，曰：「此皆百姓賣兒貼婦錢所為，佛若有知，當慈悲嗟愍；

translations.literal: Yu Yuan of Kuaiji, Attendant Gentleman of the Direct Secretariat of the Scattered Cavalry, attending at his side, said, "All this was done with money from the people selling their sons and pawning their wives; if the Buddha had knowledge, he would pity them in compassion;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan of Kuaiji, Attendant Gentleman of the Direct Secretariat, attending at his side, said, "All this was built with money from people who sold their sons and pawned their wives; if the Buddha had knowledge, he would pity them in compassion;

sentences.zh: 罪高浮圖，何功德之有！」

translations.literal: the sin towers higher than the pagoda—what merit is there!"
translations.idiomatic: the sin towers higher than the pagoda—what merit is there!"

sentences.zh: 侍坐者失色；

translations.literal: Those seated at the audience turned pale;
translations.idiomatic: Those seated at the audience turned pale;

sentences.zh: 上怒，使人驅下殿。

translations.literal: the emperor was angry and had men drive him down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor was furious and had men drive him from the hall.

sentences.zh: 願徐去，無異容。

translations.literal: Yuan departed slowly, with no change in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan withdrew slowly, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 上好圍棋，棋甚拙，與第一品彭城丞王抗圍棋，抗每假借之，曰：「皇帝飛棋，臣抗不能斷。」

translations.literal: The emperor loved playing Go; his play was quite clumsy. When he played Go with Wang Kang, Pengcheng magistrate and first rank, Kang would every time deliberately let him win, saying, "The emperor's flying stones—your servant Kang cannot cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved Go but played poorly. When he played against Wang Kang, the Pengcheng magistrate and a first-rank player, Kang always threw the game, saying, "When Your Majesty's stones fly across the board, I, Kang, cannot cut them off."

sentences.zh: 上終不悟，好之愈篤。

translations.literal: The emperor to the end did not perceive it, and loved it all the more ardently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never caught on and only grew more devoted to the game.

sentences.zh: 願又曰：「堯以此教丹朱，非人主所宜好也。」

translations.literal: Yuan also said, "Yao used this to teach Danzhu—it is not what a ruler ought to cherish."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan added, "Yao used this game to instruct Danzhu—it is not a pastime fit for a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 上雖怒甚，以願王國舊臣，每優容之。

translations.literal: Although the emperor was very angry, because Yuan was an old minister of the Wang kingdom, he always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was furious, he always showed Yuan forbearance, for Yuan had been an old minister of the Wang kingdom.

sentences.zh: 王景文常以盛滿為憂，屢辭位任，上不許。

translations.literal: Wang Jingwen constantly took fullness and overflow as a worry, repeatedly declining rank and office; the emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingwen often feared the dangers of standing too high and repeatedly tried to resign his posts, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 然中心以景文外戚貴盛，張永累經軍旅，疑其將來難信，乃自為謠言曰：「一士不可親，弓長射殺人。」

translations.literal: Yet at heart, because Jingwen as an imperial in-law was noble and flourishing, and Zhang Yong had repeatedly seen military service, he suspected that in the future they would be hard to trust; so he himself composed a catchphrase saying, "One 'shi' must not be approached—'gong' 'chang' shoots men dead."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his heart he feared that Jingwen, as a powerful imperial in-law, and Zhang Yong, a seasoned general, might prove untrustworthy in time; so he himself circulated a saying: "One 'shi' must not be approached—'gong' 'chang' shoots men dead."

sentences.zh: 景文彌懼，自表解揚州，情甚切至。

translations.literal: Jingwen grew ever more fearful and submitted a memorial requesting relief from Yangzhou; his feeling was very urgent and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen became still more terrified and memorialized the throne begging to be relieved of Yangzhou—a plea utterly desperate in tone.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「人居貴要，但問心若為耳。

translations.literal: An edict replied, saying, "When a man occupies rank and power, it is only a matter of what his heart is like.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied, "For one in high office, all that matters is the state of one's heart.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，巢、徐、二戴，位不過執戟，權亢人主。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, Chao, Xu, and the two Dais held ranks no higher than halberd-bearer, yet their power rivaled the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming reign, Chao, Xu, and the two Dai brothers held nothing more than halberd-bearer's rank, yet their power rivaled the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 今袁粲作僕射領選，而人往往不知有粲，粲遷為令，居之不疑；

translations.literal: Now Yuan Can serves as Secretary and oversees selection, yet people often do not even know that Can exists; when Can was promoted to Director, he took up the post without self-doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Today Yuan Can is Vice Director overseeing appointments, yet many barely notice he is there; when he was promoted to Director, he assumed the office without a second thought;

sentences.zh: 人情向粲，淡然亦復不改常日。

translations.literal: When popular sentiment turned toward Can, he remained indifferent and likewise did not change from his usual days.
translations.idiomatic: When favor flowed toward Can, he remained as calm and unchanged as ever.

sentences.zh: 以此居貴位要任，當有致憂競不？

translations.literal: With this, occupying high rank and vital responsibility—should there be cause for anxiety and rivalry?
translations.idiomatic: Given such conduct in high office, should one feel anxiety and rivalry?

sentences.zh: 夫貴高有危殆之懼，卑賤有填壑之憂，有心於避禍，不如無心於任運。

translations.literal: For the noble and exalted there is dread of peril; for the lowly there is fear of dying in a ditch. To set one's heart on escaping misfortune is not so good as having no heart and yielding to fate.
translations.idiomatic: The great fear peril; the humble fear starving in a ditch. A heart bent on evading disaster is not as safe as a heart that accepts whatever comes.

sentences.zh: 存亡之要，鉅細一揆耳。」

translations.literal: The essentials of survival and ruin, great and small, follow one measure."
translations.idiomatic: Whether great matters or small, the keys to survival and ruin are ultimately the same."

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝下泰豫元年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the annals of Emperor Ming Taizong, first year of Taiyu (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Ming Taizong, first year of Taiyu (

sentences.zh: 壬子，公元四七二年）

translations.literal: rénzǐ, corresponding to the year 472 CE)
translations.idiomatic: rénzǐ [sexagenary year], AD 472)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅朔，上以疾久不平，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on day jiàyín, the new moon; because the emperor's illness long had not been cured, he changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the new moon of the day jiàyín, the emperor changed the era name, his illness having long failed to abate.

sentences.zh: 戊午，皇太子會四方朝賀者於東宮，並受貢計。

translations.literal: On day wùwǔ, the crown prince assembled envoys from all quarters who had come to offer congratulations at the Eastern Palace, and together received tribute tallies.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùwǔ, the crown prince gathered congratulatory envoys from throughout the realm at the Eastern Palace and received their tribute together.

sentences.zh: 大陽蠻酋桓誕擁沔水以北、滍、葉以南八萬餘落降於魏，自雲桓玄之子，亡匿蠻中，以智略為群蠻所宗。

translations.literal: Huan Dan, chieftain of the Dayang barbarians, leading more than eighty thousand households north of the Han River and south of Zhi and Ye, surrendered to Wei. He declared himself a son of Huan Xuan; having fled and hidden among the barbarians, by strategy and cunning he was honored as leader by the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Dan, chieftain of the Dayang tribes, surrendered to Wei with more than eighty thousand households north of the Han and south of the Zhi and Ye rivers. He claimed to be a son of Huan Xuan, had hidden among the tribes, and won their allegiance through cunning.

sentences.zh: 魏以誕為征南將軍、東荊州刺史、襄陽王，聽自選郡縣吏；

translations.literal: Wei appointed Dan General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Eastern Jing Province, and Prince of Xiangyang, permitting him to choose his own county and district officials;
translations.idiomatic: Wei made Dan General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Eastern Jingzhou, and Prince of Xiangyang, allowing him to appoint his own county and district officials;

sentences.zh: 使起部郎京兆韋珍與誕安集新民，區置諸事，皆得其所。

translations.literal: It sent Lang of the Construction Bureau Wei Zhen of Jingzhao to settle the new people together with Dan; in arranging all affairs, each found its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Wei dispatched Wei Zhen of Jingzhao, a clerk of the Construction Bureau, to help Dan settle the new subjects; everything was organized to good effect.

sentences.zh: 二月，柔然侵魏，上皇遣將擊之；

translations.literal: Second month, Rouran invaded Wei; the retired emperor sent generals to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Rouran raided Wei; the retired emperor sent troops against them;

sentences.zh: 柔然走。

translations.literal: Rouran fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 東部敕勒叛奔柔然，上皇自將追之，至石磧，不及而還。

translations.literal: The eastern Tiele rebelled and fled to Rouran; the retired emperor personally led the pursuit to Shiji, failed to overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Tiele rebelled and joined the Rouran; the retired emperor led the pursuit in person as far as Shiji, failed to catch them, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 上疾篤，慮晏駕之後，皇后臨朝，江安懿侯王景文以元舅之勢，必為宰相，門族強盛，或有異圖。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness was grave. He feared that after his death, when the empress held court, Wang Jingwen, Marquis Yi of Jiang'an, with the power of the empress's eldest brother, would certainly become chief minister; his clan was powerful and flourishing, and might harbor other designs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness turned critical. He feared that once the empress regent took power, Wang Jingwen, the empress's elder brother and Marquis Yi of Jiang'an, would inevitably become chief minister—and with his clan so powerful, might entertain darker ambitions.

sentences.zh: 己未，遣使繼藥賜景文死，手敕曰：「與卿周旋，欲全卿門戶，故有此處分。」

translations.literal: On day jǐwèi, he sent an envoy with successive doses of poison to grant Jingwen death. A personal edict said, "In our dealings, I wished to preserve your whole household; therefore there is this disposition."
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐwèi, he sent an envoy bearing poison with orders that Jingwen take his own life. A personal note read, "In all our years together, I meant to protect your clan—that is why I must do this."

sentences.zh: 敕至，景文正與客棋，叩函看已，復置局下，神色不變，方與客思行爭劫。

translations.literal: When the edict arrived, Jingwen was just playing Go with a guest. He opened the casket, read it, then put it back beneath the board, his expression unchanged; he was still debating with his guest over moves in a capturing fight.
translations.idiomatic: When the order arrived, Jingwen was playing Go with a guest. He opened the box, read it, set it back under the board without altering his expression, and went on debating a capturing sequence with his guest.

sentences.zh: 局竟，斂子內奩畢，徐曰：「奉敕見賜以死。」

translations.literal: When the game ended, he gathered the stones into the inner casket; then he said slowly, "By edict I am granted death."
translations.idiomatic: When the game ended, he put the stones away in their box and said calmly, "By imperial order, I am commanded to die."

sentences.zh: 方以敕示客。

translations.literal: Then he showed the edict to his guest.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he show the order to his guest.

sentences.zh: 中直兵焦度趙智略憤怒，曰：「大丈夫安能坐受死！

translations.literal: The Central Direct Guardsmen Jiao Du and Zhao Zhilue, furious, said, "A true man—how can he sit and accept death!
translations.idiomatic: His Central Direct Guardsmen Jiao Du and Zhao Zhilue erupted in rage: "What sort of man sits still and accepts death!

sentences.zh: 州中文武數百，足以一奮。」

translations.literal: Within the province, civil and military officials number in the hundreds—enough for one bold stroke."
translations.idiomatic: The province holds hundreds of civil and military officers—more than enough for us to strike back."

sentences.zh: 景文曰：「知卿至心；

translations.literal: Jingwen said, "I know your utmost loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen said, "I know your heart is true;

sentences.zh: 若見念者，為我百口計。」

translations.literal: If you would spare a thought for me, plan for my hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: If you care for me at all, look to the safety of my entire household."

sentences.zh: 乃作墨啟答敕致謝，飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote an ink reply to the edict expressing thanks, drank the poison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a brief reply thanking the emperor, drank the poison, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master with Golden Seal and Tripartite Equal Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Threefold Honorific Equivalence.

sentences.zh: 上夢有人告曰：「豫章太守劉愔反。」

translations.literal: The emperor dreamed that someone reported, saying, "Liu Yin, Administrator of Yuzhang, has rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dreamed that someone told him, "Liu Yin, Administrator of Yuzhang, is in rebellion."

sentences.zh: 既寤，遣人就郡殺之。

translations.literal: When he awoke, he sent men to the commandery to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: On waking, he sent men to the commandery and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 魏顯祖還平城。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu of Wei returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu of Wei returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 庚午，魏主耕籍田。

translations.literal: On day gēngwǔ, the Wei sovereign plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngwǔ, the Wei emperor performed the spring plowing rite in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以垣崇祖行徐州事，徙戍龍沮。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Yuan Chongzu was appointed to administer Xuzhou affairs and was transferred to garrison Longju.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Yuan Chongzu was put in charge of Xuzhou and transferred to garrison Longju.

sentences.zh: 己亥，上大漸，以江州刺史桂陽王休范為司空，又以尚書右僕射褚淵為護軍將軍，加中領軍劉勉右僕射，詔淵、勉與尚書令袁粲、荊州刺史蔡興宗、郢州刺史沈攸之並受顧命。

translations.literal: On day jǐhài, as the emperor's condition worsened, he made Prince Guiyang, Xu Fan, Governor of Jiangzhou, Grand Master of Works; made Chu Yuan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Guardian General; promoted Liu Mian, Central Army Commander, to Vice Director; and decreed that Chu, Liu, Director Yuan Can, Governor Cai Xingzong of Jingzhou, and Governor Shen Youzhi of Yingzhou would all receive the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐhài, as the emperor lay dying, he made Prince Guiyang Xu Fan, Governor of Jiangzhou, Grand Master of Works; made Chu Yuan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Guardian General; promoted Central Army Commander Liu Mian to Vice Director; and decreed that Chu, Liu, Director Yuan Can, Jingzhou Governor Cai Xingzong, and Yingzhou Governor Shen Youzhi would all receive the dying emperor's testament.

sentences.zh: 褚淵素與蕭道成善，引薦於上，詔又以道成為右衛將軍，領衛尉，與袁粲等共掌機事。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan had long been on good terms with Xiao Daocheng and recommended him to the emperor; an edict also made Daocheng Right Guard General, concurrently Commandant of the Guard, sharing control of state affairs with Yuan Can and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan had long been friendly with Xiao Daocheng and recommended him to the throne; an edict also made Daocheng Right Guard General and Commandant of the Guard, sharing control of state affairs with Yuan Can and the others.

sentences.zh: 是夕，上殂。

translations.literal: That very night, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That very night, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On day gēngzǐ, the crown prince ascended the throne as emperor and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngzǐ, the crown prince ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 時蒼梧王方十歲，袁粲、褚淵秉政，承太宗奢侈之後，務弘節儉，欲救其弊；
