translations.literal: The Lord of Cangwu was then only ten years old. Yuan Can and Chu Yuan held the reins of government; inheriting the extravagance after Emperor Taizong, they strove to promote thrift and remedy the abuses;
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Cangwu was then only ten. Yuan Can and Chu Yuan held the reins of government; coming after Emperor Taizong's extravagance, they strove to promote thrift and remedy the abuses;

sentences.zh: 而阮佃夫、王道隆等用事，貨賂公行，不能禁也。

translations.literal: Yet Ruan Tainfu, Wang Daolong, and others held power; bribery was openly practiced, and they could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ruan Tainfu, Wang Daolong, and their faction held sway; bribery ran rampant, and nothing could be done to stop it.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以安成王准為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: On day yǐsì, Prince Ancheng, Liu Zhun, was made Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yǐsì, Prince Ancheng Liu Zhun was appointed Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊寅，葬明皇帝於高寧陵，廟號太宗。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on day wùyín, Emperor Ming was buried at Gaoning Mausoleum; his temple name was Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day wùyín, Emperor Ming was buried at Gaoning Mausoleum and given the temple name Taizong.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙巳，尊皇后曰皇太后，立妃江氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on day yǐsì, the empress was honored as empress dowager, and Consort Jiang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day yǐsì, the empress was honored as empress dowager and Consort Jiang was made empress.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，柔然部帥無盧真將三萬騎寇魏敦煌，鎮將尉多侯擊走之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Rouran chieftain Wulu Zhen led thirty thousand horsemen to raid Dunhuang in Wei; the garrison commander Yuduohou drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, the Rouran chieftain Wulu Zhen led thirty thousand horsemen against Dunhuang in Wei; garrison commander Yuduohou drove them off.

sentences.zh: 多侯，眷之子也。

translations.literal: Yuduohou was the son of Juan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuduohou was the son of Juan.

sentences.zh: 又寇晉昌，守將薛奴擊走之。

translations.literal: They again raided Jinchang; the defending general Xue Nu drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Jinchang as well; defending general Xue Nu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On day wùwǔ, the Wei sovereign went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùwǔ, the Wei emperor went to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，尊帝母陳貴妃為皇太妃，更以諸國太妃為太姬。

translations.literal: On day wùchén, the emperor's mother, Consort Chen, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort; the title of imperial consorts of the various kingdoms was changed to Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùchén, the emperor's mother, Consort Chen, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort, and the title of imperial consorts of the various kingdoms was changed to Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍王道隆以蔡興宗強直，不欲使居上流，閏月，甲辰，以興宗為中書監；

translations.literal: Right Army General Wang Daolong, because Cai Xingzong was stern and upright, did not wish him to hold the upper reaches; in the intercalary month, on day jiǎchén, Xingzong was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: Right Army General Wang Daolong, finding Cai Xingzong too stern and upright to keep on the upper Yangzi, made him Supervisor of the Masters of Writing in the intercalary month on the day jiǎchén;

sentences.zh: 更以沈攸之為都督荊、襄等八州諸軍事、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi was instead made Commander-in-Chief over military affairs of the eight provinces including Jing and Xiang, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi was instead made Commander-in-Chief over the eight provinces including Jing and Xiang, and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 興宗辭中書監不拜。

translations.literal: Xingzong declined the post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong declined the post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 王道隆每詣興宗，躡履到前，不敢就席，良久去，竟不呼坐。

translations.literal: Whenever Wang Daolong called on Xingzong, he would tiptoe forward in his shoes, not daring to take a seat; after a long while he would leave, and in the end Xingzong never invited him to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Daolong visited Xingzong, he would tiptoe forward and stand before him, not daring to take a seat; after a long while he would leave—and Xingzong never once asked him to sit.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之自以才略過人，自至夏口以來，陰蓄異志；

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi considered his talent and strategy to surpass others; from the time he reached Xiakou onward, he secretly harbored other designs;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi considered himself more talented and capable than anyone else; from the time he reached Xiakou, he had secretly nursed other ambitions;

sentences.zh: 及徙荊州，擇郢州士馬、器仗精者，多以自隨。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Jingzhou, he selected the finest soldiers, horses, and weapons of Yingzhou and took most of them with him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Jingzhou, he picked out Yingzhou's best troops, horses, and arms and took most of them with him.

sentences.zh: 到官，以討蠻為名，大發兵力，招聚才勇，部勒嚴整，常如敵至。

translations.literal: On taking office, under the pretext of campaigning against the barbarians, he mustered troops on a large scale, gathered men of talent and courage, and drilled them with strict discipline, always as if the enemy were at hand.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office, he raised troops on a large scale under the pretext of campaigning against the tribes, gathered talented and brave men, and drilled them with such strict discipline that it was as if the enemy were always at the gates.

sentences.zh: 重賦斂以繕器甲，舊應供台者皆割留之，養馬至二千餘匹，治戰艦近千艘，倉廩、府庫莫不充積。

translations.literal: He imposed heavy levies to repair armor and weapons; what by custom should have been sent to the capital he retained; he raised horses to more than two thousand head, built nearly a thousand warships, and filled every granary and treasury to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed heavy taxes to repair armor and weapons, kept for himself everything that should have gone to the capital, raised more than two thousand horses, built nearly a thousand warships, and filled every granary and treasury to overflowing.

sentences.zh: 士子、商旅過荊州者，多為所羈留；

translations.literal: Scholars and traveling merchants passing through Jingzhou were often detained by him;
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and traveling merchants passing through Jingzhou were often detained by him;

sentences.zh: 四方亡命歸之者，皆蔽匿擁護；

translations.literal: Fugitives from all quarters who came to join him were all sheltered and protected;
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives from all quarters who came to him were sheltered and protected;

sentences.zh: 所部或有逃亡，無遠近窮追，必得而止。

translations.literal: If anyone under his command fled, he pursued them without regard to distance until they were caught.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone under his command fled, he pursued them without regard to distance until they were caught.

sentences.zh: 舉錯專恣，不復承用符敕，朝廷疑而憚之。

translations.literal: His actions were arbitrary and wilful; he no longer obeyed edicts and orders from the court, and the court both suspected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He acted with arbitrary wilfulness, no longer heeding edicts from the court, which both suspected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 為政刻暴，或鞭撻士大夫；

translations.literal: In governing he was harsh and cruel, sometimes flogging scholar-officials;
translations.idiomatic: His rule was harsh and cruel; he sometimes flogged scholar-officials;

sentences.zh: 上佐以下，面加詈辱。

translations.literal: From senior aides downward, he would revile and humiliate them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: and from senior aides downward he would revile and humiliate men to their faces.

sentences.zh: 然吏事精明，人不敢欺，境內盜賊屏息，夜戶不閉。

translations.literal: Yet in administrative matters he was sharp and precise; no one dared deceive him; within his borders bandits fell silent, and at night people did not lock their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was sharp and precise in administrative matters; no one dared deceive him; bandits fell silent within his borders, and at night people left their doors unlatched.

sentences.zh: 攸之賧罰群蠻太甚，又禁五溪魚鹽，蠻怨叛。

translations.literal: Youzhi's fines and punishments on the tribal peoples were too severe, and he also banned fish and salt in the Five Streams region; the tribes resented this and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's fines and punishments on the tribal peoples were excessive, and he also banned the trade in fish and salt in the Five Streams region; the tribes rebelled in resentment.

sentences.zh: 酉溪蠻王田頭擬死，弟婁侯篡立，其子田都走入獠中。

translations.literal: Tian Touni, king of the Youxi tribes, died; his younger brother Louhou seized the throne by usurpation, and his son Tian Du fled into the Liao tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Touni, king of the Youxi tribes, died; his younger brother Louhou usurped the throne, and his son Tian Du fled among the Liao tribes.

sentences.zh: 於是群蠻大亂，掠抄至武陵城下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the tribes fell into great disorder and plundered as far as the walls of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes then erupted in chaos and raided all the way to the walls of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 武陵內史蕭嶷遣隊主張英兒擊破之，誅婁佩，立田都，群蠻乃定。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan, Administrator of Wuling, sent Squad Leader Zhang Ying'er to defeat them, executed Lou Pei, installed Tian Du, and the tribes were then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan, Administrator of Wuling, sent Squad Leader Zhang Ying'er to defeat them, executed Louhou, installed Tian Du, and the tribes were pacified.

sentences.zh: 嶷，賾之弟也。

translations.literal: Yan was the younger brother of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was the younger brother of Ze.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，樂安宣穆公蔡興宗卒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on day wùwǔ, Cai Xingzong, Duke Xuanmu of Le'an, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day wùwǔ, Cai Xingzong, Duke Xuanmu of Le'an, died.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on day xīnsì, the Wei sovereign returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day xīnsì, the Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，柔然侵魏，及五原。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Rouran invaded Wei and reached Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, the Rouran invaded Wei and reached Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上皇自將討之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, the retired emperor personally led a campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, the retired emperor led a campaign against them in person.

sentences.zh: 將度漠，柔然北走數千里，上皇乃還。

translations.literal: As he was about to cross the desert, Rouran fled north for several thousand li; the retired emperor then returned.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to cross the desert, the Rouran fled north for thousands of li; the retired emperor then turned back.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏封上皇之弟略為文川王。

translations.literal: On day dīnghài, Wei enfeoffed the retired emperor's younger brother Lüe as Prince of Wenchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dīnghài, Wei enfeoffed the retired emperor's younger brother Lüe as Prince of Wenchuan.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以郢州刺史劉秉為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On day jǐhài, Liu Bing, Governor of Yingzhou, was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐhài, Yingzhou Governor Liu Bing was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秉，道憐之孫也，和弱無干能，以宗室清令，故袁、褚引之。

translations.literal: Bing was the grandson of Dao'ai; gentle and weak, without practical ability, but because as a member of the imperial clan he was pure and distinguished, Yuan and Chu brought him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was the grandson of Dao'ai—gentle, mild, and without practical ability—but as a pure and distinguished member of the imperial clan, Yuan and Chu brought him forward.

sentences.zh: 中書通事舍人阮佃夫加給事中、輔國將軍，權任轉重，欲用其所親吳郡張澹為武陵郡；

translations.literal: Ruan Tainfu, Attendant Master of Communications of the Secretariat, was additionally made Palace Attendant and General Who Assists the State; his power and responsibility grew ever heavier. He wished to appoint his close associate Zhang Dan of Wu Commandery as Administrator of Wuling;
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tainfu, Attendant Master of Communications of the Secretariat, was additionally made Palace Attendant and General Who Assists the State; his power grew ever heavier. He wished to appoint his protégé Zhang Dan of Wu Commandery as Administrator of Wuling;

sentences.zh: 袁粲等皆不同，佃夫稱敕施行，粲等不敢執。

translations.literal: Yuan Can and the others all disagreed, but Tainfu declared that an edict ordered it carried out; Can and the others did not dare insist.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and the others all objected, but Tainfu claimed an edict and pushed the appointment through; Can and the others did not dare stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 魏有司奏諸祠祀合一千七十五所，歲用牲七萬五千五百。

translations.literal: The Wei authorities reported that sacrificial sites altogether numbered one thousand seventy-five, and each year they consumed seventy-five thousand five hundred sacrificial animals.
translations.idiomatic: Wei officials reported that sacrificial sites numbered one thousand seventy-five in all, consuming seventy-five thousand five hundred sacrificial animals each year.

sentences.zh: 上皇惡其多殺，詔：「自今非天地、宗廟、社稷，皆勿用牲，薦以酒脯而已。」

translations.literal: The retired emperor hated the great slaughter; he decreed, "From now on, except for Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain, do not use sacrificial animals; offer wine and dried meat only."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor deplored the slaughter and decreed, "From now on, except for rites to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain, no sacrificial animals shall be used—wine and dried meat will suffice."

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝下元徽元年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the annals of Emperor Ming Taizong, first year of Yuanhui (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Ming Taizong, first year of Yuanhui (

sentences.zh: 癸丑，公元四七三年）

translations.literal: guǐchǒu, corresponding to the year 473 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guǐchǒu [sexagenary year], AD 473)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊寅朔，改元，大赦。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on day wùyín, the new moon; the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the new moon of the day wùyín, the era name was changed and a general amnesty proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，魏員外散騎常侍崔演來聘。

translations.literal: On day gēngchén, Cui Yan of Wei, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gēngchén, Cui Yan of Wei, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, came on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，魏上皇還，至雲中。

translations.literal: On day wùxū, the retired emperor of Wei returned and reached Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùxū, the retired emperor of Wei returned and reached Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，魏詔守令勸課農事，同部之內，貧富相通，家有兼牛，通借無者。

translations.literal: On day guǐchǒu, Wei decreed that prefects and magistrates should encourage agricultural work: within the same district, rich and poor should assist one another—households with extra oxen should lend them to those without.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guǐchǒu, Wei decreed that prefects and magistrates should promote agriculture: within each district, rich and poor were to help one another—households with spare oxen were to lend them to those who had none.

sentences.zh: 若不從詔，一門終身不仕。

translations.literal: If they did not obey the decree, the whole household would be barred from office for life.
translations.idiomatic: Those who disobeyed would see their entire household barred from office for life.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏上皇至平城。

translations.literal: On day wùwǔ, the retired emperor of Wei reached Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wùwǔ, the retired emperor of Wei reached Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏詔：「縣令能靜一縣劫盜者，兼治二縣，即食其祿；

translations.literal: On day jiǎxū, Wei decreed, "A magistrate who can pacify banditry in one county shall concurrently administer two counties and receive both salaries;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiǎxū, Wei decreed, "A magistrate who can pacify banditry in one county shall concurrently administer two counties and draw both salaries;

sentences.zh: 能靜二縣者，兼治三縣，三年遷為郡守。

translations.literal: One who can pacify two counties shall concurrently administer three counties, and after three years be promoted to commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: One who can pacify two counties shall concurrently administer three, and after three years be promoted to commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 二千石能靜二郡上至三郡亦如之，三年遷為刺史。」

translations.literal: A two-thousand-dan official who can pacify two commanderies, up to three commanderies, shall likewise be promoted after three years to regional inspector."
translations.idiomatic: A two-thousand-dan official who can pacify two commanderies—or up to three—shall likewise be promoted after three years to regional inspector.”

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休范，素凡訥，少知解，不為諸兄所齒遇，物情亦不向之，故太宗之末得免於禍。

translations.literal: Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang had always been mediocre and slow-witted, with little understanding; his elder brothers did not treat him as an equal, and public sentiment likewise did not favor him, so at the end of Emperor Taizong's reign he was spared from calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang was a dull, slow-witted man with little learning; his elder brothers looked down on him, and the world paid him no regard—so when Emperor Taizong's reign drew to its end, he alone escaped the calamities that struck others.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，年在沖幼，素族秉政，近習用權。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne he was still very young; members of the imperial clan held power, and close attendants wielded authority.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor was still a child; the imperial clan wielded government, and favored attendants held the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 休范自謂尊親莫二，應入為宰輔；

translations.literal: Xiufan considered himself second to none in rank and closeness to the throne and believed he ought to enter the capital as chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan believed that in rank and kinship none stood above him, and that he deserved to enter the capital as chief minister;

sentences.zh: 既不如志，怨憤頗甚。

translations.literal: When he failed to achieve his ambition, his resentment grew very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Denied what he sought, his resentment festered.

sentences.zh: 典簽新蔡許公輿為之謀主，令休范折節下士，厚相資給。

translations.literal: His bureau secretary Xu Gongyu of Xincai served as his chief strategist, urging Xiufan to humble himself before men of talent and generously support them with funds.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gongyu of Xincai, his bureau secretary, became his chief strategist and urged him to humble himself before worthy men and support them generously.

sentences.zh: 於是遠近赴之，歲中萬計；

translations.literal: Men from near and far then flocked to him, numbering in the tens of thousands within a year;
translations.idiomatic: Men from every quarter then gathered at his door; within a year they numbered in the tens of thousands;

sentences.zh: 收養勇士，繕治器械。

translations.literal: He gathered brave fighters and repaired weapons and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He took in bold warriors and put arms and equipment in order.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其有異志，亦陰為之備。

translations.literal: The court knew he harbored rebellious intentions and secretly made preparations against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court perceived his rebellious designs and quietly made ready against him.

sentences.zh: 會夏口闕鎮，朝廷以其地居尋陽上流，欲使腹心居之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Xiakou garrison post fell vacant; because the place lay upstream from Xunyang, the court wished to station a trusted man there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiakou garrison post fell vacant, the court—because the place lay upstream from Xunyang—wished to place a trusted man there.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙亥，以晉熙王燮為郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yǐhài, Prince Liu Xie of Jinxi was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yǐhài, Prince Liu Xie of Jinxi was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 燮始四歲，以黃門郎王奐為長史，行府州事，配以資力，使鎮夏口；

translations.literal: Xie was only four years old; Wang Huan, a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was made Chief Administrator to handle the prefecture and provincial affairs, and with sufficient resources was sent to garrison Xiakou;
translations.idiomatic: Xie was but four years old; Wang Huan, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was appointed Chief Administrator to govern the prefecture and province, given adequate resources, and sent to hold Xiakou;

sentences.zh: 復恐其過尋陽為休范所劫留，使自太洑徑去。

translations.literal: The court also feared that passing Xunyang he might be seized and detained by Xiufan, so he was sent to go directly via Taipu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he might be seized and held by Xiufan if he passed through Xunyang, the court ordered him to go directly by way of Taipu.

sentences.zh: 休范聞之，大怒，密與許公輿謀襲建康；

translations.literal: When Xiufan heard of this, he flew into a rage and secretly plotted with Xu Gongyu to strike Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan learned of this he was enraged, and secretly plotted with Xu Gongyu to strike Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 表治城湟，多解材板而蓄之。

translations.literal: He claimed to be repairing the city moat and stockpiled timber and planks in large quantities.
translations.idiomatic: He announced that he was repairing the city moat while secretly stockpiling timber and planks in vast quantities.

sentences.zh: 奐，景文之兄子也。

translations.literal: Huan was the nephew of Wang Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was Wang Jingwen's nephew.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王拾寅寇魏澆河。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun King Shiyin raided Jiaohe in Wei territory.
translations.idiomatic: King Shiyin of Tuyuhun raided Jiaohe in Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，魏以司空長孫觀為大都督，發兵討之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day wùshēn, Wei appointed Grand Guardian Changsun Guan Grand Commander and dispatched troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on wùshēn, Wei made Grand Guardian Changsun Guan Grand Commander and sent troops against him.

sentences.zh: 魏以孔子二十八世孫乘為崇聖大夫，給十戶以供灑掃。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Kong Cheng, twenty-eighth-generation descendant of Confucius, as Sage-Venerating Grand Master, with ten households assigned to supply sacrificial sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Kong Cheng, twenty-eighth-generation descendant of Confucius, Sage-Venerating Grand Master, assigning ten households to maintain the rites of sweeping and tending the shrine.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏詔：「河南六州之民，戶收絹一匹，綿一斤，租三十石。」

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wei decreed: "For the people of the six Henan provinces, each household shall pay one bolt of silk, one jin of cotton, and thirty shi of grain rent."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wei issued an edict: "For households in the six Henan provinces, each shall pay one bolt of silk, one jin of cotton, and thirty shi of grain as rent.”

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏主如陰山。

translations.literal: On the day yǐhài, the Wei emperor went to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: On yǐhài the Wei emperor traveled to Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，魏上皇如河西。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day gēngshēn, the retired emperor of Wei went to Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gēngshēn, the retired emperor of Wei went to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 長孫觀入吐谷渾境，芻其秋稼。

translations.literal: Changsun Guan entered Tuyuhun territory and cut down their autumn crops for fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Guan crossed into Tuyuhun territory and reaped their autumn grain for fodder.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王拾寅窘急，請降，遣子斤入侍。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun King Shiyin, hard pressed, requested surrender and sent his son Jin to serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: King Shiyin of Tuyuhun, cornered, asked to surrender and sent his son Jin to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 自是歲修職貢。

translations.literal: From then on he paid tribute every year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he sent tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，上皇還平城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xīnsì, the retired emperor returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xīnsì, the retired emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 遣使如魏。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched envoys to Wei.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉，割南兗、豫州之境置徐州，治鐘離。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day guǐyǒu, territory was carved from southern Yanzhou and Yuzhou to establish Xuzhou, with its seat at Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on guǐyǒu, lands were carved from southern Yanzhou and Yuzhou to create Xuzhou, seated at Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 魏上皇將入寇，詔州郡之民十丁取一以充行，戶收租五十石以備軍糧。

translations.literal: The retired emperor of Wei was about to invade; he decreed that one man in ten from the people of the provinces and commanderies be conscripted for the campaign, and each household pay fifty shi of grain rent to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: As the retired emperor of Wei prepared to launch an invasion, he decreed that one man in ten from the provinces and commanderies be drafted for the campaign, and that each household furnish fifty shi of grain to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 魏武都氐反，攻仇池，詔長孫觀回師討之。

translations.literal: The Di of Wudu in Wei rebelled and attacked Chouchi; the court ordered Changsun Guan to withdraw and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Di people of Wudu in Wei rose in rebellion and attacked Chouchi; the court ordered Changsun Guan to withdraw and put them down.

sentences.zh: 武都王楊僧嗣卒於葭蘆，從弟文度自立為武興王，遣使降魏；

translations.literal: Prince Yang Sengsi of Wudu died at Jialu; his younger cousin Wen Du proclaimed himself King of Wuxing and sent envoys to surrender to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang Sengsi of Wudu died at Jialu; his younger cousin Wen Du declared himself King of Wuxing and sent envoys to submit to Wei;

sentences.zh: 魏以文度為武興鎮將。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Wen Du as Garrison Commander of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named Wen Du Garrison Commander of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁丑，尚書令袁粲以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day dīngchǒu, Yuan Can, Director of the Department of State Affairs, left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dīngchǒu, Yuan Can, Director of the Department of State Affairs, resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，魏上皇南巡，至懷州。

translations.literal: On the day guǐsì, the retired emperor of Wei made a southern tour and reached Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guǐsì the retired emperor of Wei made a southern progress and reached Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 枋頭鎮將代人薛虎子，先為馮太后所黜，為門士。

translations.literal: Xue Huzi of Dai, former garrison commander at Fangtou, had previously been dismissed by Empress Dowager Feng and reduced to a gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huzi of Dai, who had once been garrison commander at Fangtou, had been dismissed by Empress Dowager Feng and reduced to a gate guard.

sentences.zh: 時山東饑，盜賊競起，相州民孫誨等五百人稱虎子在鎮，境內清晏，乞還虎子。

translations.literal: At that time east of the mountains famine prevailed and bandits rose everywhere; five hundred men of Xiangzhou led by Sun Hui and others declared that while Huzi had been at the garrison the region had been peaceful, and petitioned for his restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the lands east of the mountains and bandits sprang up everywhere; five hundred men of Xiangzhou, led by Sun Hui and others, testified that under Huzi the frontier had been quiet and begged that he be restored.

sentences.zh: 上皇復以虎子為枋頭鎮將，即日之官，數州盜賊皆息。

translations.literal: The retired emperor reappointed Huzi as garrison commander at Fangtou; he took office the same day, and banditry ceased across several provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor restored Huzi to command at Fangtou; he took up his post that same day, and banditry subsided across several provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of the day guǐmǎo, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of guǐmǎo, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，江州刺史桂陽王休范進位太尉。

translations.literal: On the day yǐsì, Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yǐsì Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was elevated to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 詔起袁粲，以衛軍將軍攝職，粲固辭。

translations.literal: An edict recalled Yuan Can, appointing him General of the Guard to act in the post; Yuan firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Yuan Can back, appointing him General of the Guard to serve in the post; Yuan refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 壬子，柔然侵魏，柔玄鎮二部敕勒應之。

translations.literal: On the day rénzǐ, Rouran invaded Wei; the two divisions of Chilie at Rouxuan garrison responded.
translations.idiomatic: On rénzǐ Rouran invaded Wei; the two Chilie divisions at Rouxuan garrison marched to meet them.

sentences.zh: 魏州鎮十一水旱，相州民餓死者二千八百餘人。

translations.literal: Eleven provinces and garrisons in Wei suffered floods and drought; more than twenty-eight hundred people starved to death in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven provinces and garrisons in Wei suffered flood and drought; in Xiangzhou alone more than twenty-eight hundred people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏妖人劉舉聚眾自稱天子。

translations.literal: That year, the sorcerer Liu Ju of Wei gathered a crowd and proclaimed himself Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year the sorcerer Liu Ju of Wei gathered followers and declared himself Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 劉州刺史武昌王平原討斬之。

translations.literal: Prince Liu Pingyuan of Wuchang, Inspector of Liuzhou, attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Pingyuan of Wuchang, Inspector of Liuzhou, attacked him and took his head.

sentences.zh: 平原，提之子也。

translations.literal: Pingyuan was the son of Liu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan was Liu Ti's son.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝下元徽二年（

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming Taizong, second year of Yuanhui (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Ming Taizong, second year of Yuanhui (

sentences.zh: 甲寅，公元四七四年）

translations.literal: jiǎyín [sexagenary year], AD 474)
translations.idiomatic: jiǎyín of the sexagenary cycle, AD 474)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁丑，魏太尉源賀以疾罷。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the day dīngchǒu, Yuan He, Grand Commander of Wei, was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on dīngchǒu, Yuan He, Grand Commander of Wei, was relieved of office because of illness.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲辰，魏上皇還平城。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day jiǎchén, the retired emperor of Wei returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiǎchén, the retired emperor of Wei came back to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁亥，魏員外散騎常侍許赤虎來聘。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day dīnghài, Xu Chihu of Wei, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, came on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dīnghài, Xu Chihu of Wei, Supernumerary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, arrived on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬午，桂陽王休范反。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day rénwǔ, Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on rénwǔ, Prince Liu Xiufan of Guiyang rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 掠民船，使軍隊稱力請受，付以材板，合乎裝治。

translations.literal: He seized civilian boats and had his troops call out offering payment for transport, then handed over timber and planks for them to assemble and fit out.
translations.idiomatic: He commandeered civilian boats; his troops called out, offering payment for transport, and supplied timber and planks for the owners to fit out their vessels.

sentences.zh: 數日即辦。

translations.literal: Within a few days all was ready.
translations.idiomatic: Within days everything was ready.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，休范帥眾二萬、騎五百發尋陽，晝夜取道；

translations.literal: On the day bǐngxū, Xiufan led twenty thousand foot soldiers and five hundred cavalry out from Xunyang, pressing forward day and night;
translations.idiomatic: On bǐngxū Xiufan marched out of Xunyang at the head of twenty thousand foot soldiers and five hundred cavalry, pressing forward without rest day or night;

sentences.zh: 以書與諸執政，稱：「楊運長、王道隆蠱惑先帝，使建安、巴陵二王無罪被戮。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to the chief ministers, stating: "Yang Yunchang and Wang Daolong beguiled the late emperor and caused the Princes of Jian'an and Baling to be executed though guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to the chief ministers, saying: "Yang Yunchang and Wang Daolong misled the late emperor and brought about the execution of the Princes of Jian'an and Baling though they were innocent.

sentences.zh: 望執錄二豎，以謝冤魂。」

translations.literal: I hope you will seize and capture these two villains to appease the wronged dead."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you seize these two villains and offer their deaths to the spirits of the wronged.”

sentences.zh: 庚寅，大雷戍主杜道欣馳下告變，朝廷惶駭。

translations.literal: On the day gēngyín, Du Daoxin, commander of the Dalei garrison, rode down posthaste to report the uprising, and the court was stricken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: On gēngyín Du Daoxin, commander of the Dalei garrison, galloped down with news of the revolt, and panic seized the court.

sentences.zh: 護軍褚淵、征北將軍張永、領軍劉勉、僕射劉秉、右衛將軍蕭道成、游擊將軍載明寶、驍騎將軍阮佃夫、右軍將軍王道隆、中書舍人孫千齡、員外郎楊運長集中書省計事，莫有言者。

translations.literal: Guardian of the Army Chu Yuan, Commander of the North Zhang Yong, Commander of the Capital Guard Liu Mian, Vice Director Liu Bing, Right Guard General Xiao Daocheng, Mobile Corps General Zai Mingbao, Valiant Cavalry General Ruan Tianfu, Right Army General Wang Daolong, Secretariat Attendant Sun Qianling, and Supernumerary Gentleman Yang Yunchang gathered at the Secretariat to deliberate, and none spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, Guardian of the Army; Zhang Yong, Commander of the North; Liu Mian, Commander of the Capital Guard; Liu Bing, Vice Director; Xiao Daocheng, Right Guard General; Zai Mingbao, Mobile Corps General; Ruan Tianfu, Valiant Cavalry General; Wang Daolong, Right Army General; Sun Qianling, Secretariat Attendant; and Yang Yunchang, Supernumerary Gentleman—all gathered at the Secretariat to deliberate, and not one spoke.

sentences.zh: 道成曰：「昔上流謀逆，皆因淹緩致敗。

translations.literal: Daocheng said: "In the past, rebellions from upstream all failed because our response was too slow.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said: "Rebellions from upstream have failed in the past precisely because we responded too slowly.

sentences.zh: 休范必遠懲前失，輕兵急下，乘我無備。

translations.literal: Xiufan will surely take the earlier failures as a distant lesson and come down in light force with all speed, catching us unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan will heed those earlier failures from afar and come down in a light, swift force to catch us off guard.

sentences.zh: 今應變之術，不宜遠出；

translations.literal: The art of meeting this crisis is not to march far out;
translations.idiomatic: The way to meet this crisis is not to march far afield;

sentences.zh: 若偏師失律，則大沮眾心。

translations.literal: if a detached force loses discipline, it will gravely dispirit the troops.
translations.idiomatic: if a detached column loses discipline, it will crush the army's spirit.

sentences.zh: 宜頓新亭、白下，堅守宮城、東府、石頭，以待賊至。

translations.literal: We should halt at Xinting and Baixia, hold fast the palace city, the Eastern Secretariat, and Shitou, and wait for the rebels to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: We should hold Xinting and Baixia, stand firm at the palace city, the Eastern Secretariat, and Shitou, and wait for the rebels to arrive.

sentences.zh: 千里孤軍，後無委積，求戰不得，自然瓦解。

translations.literal: An army a thousand li from home, with no supplies behind it, unable to force a battle—it will collapse of itself.
translations.idiomatic: An army a thousand li from home, with no supplies in its rear and no chance to force a battle, will fall apart on its own.

sentences.zh: 我請頓新亭以當其鋒。

translations.literal: I ask to hold Xinting and take their charge head-on.
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to hold Xinting and meet their vanguard head-on.

sentences.zh: 征北守白下，領軍屯宣陽門為諸軍節度；

translations.literal: The Commander of the North shall guard Baixia; the Commander of the Capital Guard shall camp at Xuanyang Gate to direct all armies;
translations.idiomatic: The Commander of the North shall hold Baixia; the Commander of the Capital Guard shall encamp at Xuanyang Gate and direct the armies;

sentences.zh: 諸貴安坐殿中，不須競出，我自破賊必矣！」

translations.literal: You nobles may sit quietly in the hall without rushing out—I shall surely break the rebels myself!"
translations.idiomatic: You nobles may sit at ease in the hall without rushing forth—I myself will surely break the rebels!"

sentences.zh: 因索筆下議。

translations.literal: He then asked for a brush and wrote down the plan for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He then called for a brush and wrote out the plan for the assembly to approve.

sentences.zh: 眾並注「同」。

translations.literal: All annotated "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wrote "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 孫千齡陰與休范通謀，獨曰：「宜依舊遣軍據梁山。」

translations.literal: Sun Qianling, secretly in league with Xiufan, alone said: "We should as before dispatch troops to hold Liangshan."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qianling, secretly in league with Xiufan, alone objected: "We should, as before, send troops to hold Liangshan."

sentences.zh: 道成正色曰：「賊今已近，梁山豈可得至！

translations.literal: Daocheng said sternly: "The rebels are already near—how could we even reach Liangshan!
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said with a stern face: "The rebels are already close—how could we even reach Liangshan!

sentences.zh: 新亭既是兵沖，所欲以死報國耳。

translations.literal: Since Xinting is the military chokepoint, what I want is to repay the state with my death.
translations.idiomatic: Xinting is the military chokepoint; what I intend is to repay the state with my life.

sentences.zh: 常時乃可屈曲相從，今不得也！」

translations.literal: At ordinary times one might bend and follow along; not now!"
translations.idiomatic: At other times one might yield and go along—not now!"

sentences.zh: 坐起，道成顧謂劉勉曰：「領軍已同鄙議，不可改易！」

translations.literal: He rose from his seat. Daocheng turned to Liu Mian and said: "The Commander of the Capital Guard has already agreed with my view—it cannot be changed!"
translations.idiomatic: He stood up. Daocheng turned to Liu Mian and said: "The Commander of the Capital Guard has already agreed with my plan—it cannot be changed!"

sentences.zh: 袁粲聞難，扶曳入殿。

translations.literal: Yuan Can, hearing of the crisis, was helped and dragged into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can, hearing of the emergency, was helped and dragged into the hall.

sentences.zh: 即日，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: That same day, martial law was declared within and without.
translations.idiomatic: That same day martial law was proclaimed within and without the capital.

sentences.zh: 道成將前鋒兵出屯新亭，張永屯白下，前南兗州刺史沈懷明戍石頭，袁粲、褚淵入衛殿省。

translations.literal: Daocheng led the vanguard out to camp at Xinting; Zhang Yong camped at Baixia; Shen Huaiming, former Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, garrisoned Shitou; Yuan Can and Chu Yuan entered to guard the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng led the vanguard out to encamp at Xinting; Zhang Yong encamped at Baixia; Shen Huaiming, former Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, garrisoned Shitou; Yuan Can and Chu Yuan entered to defend the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 時侖猝，不暇授甲，開南北二武庫，隨將士意所取。

translations.literal: Time was urgent and there was no leisure to issue armor; the northern and southern arsenals were opened and the officers and men took what they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Time was short and there was no leisure to distribute armor; the northern and southern arsenals were thrown open and officers and men took what they needed.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成至新亭，治城壘未畢，辛卯，休范前軍已至新林。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng reached Xinting; before the fortifications were finished, on the day xīnmǎo Xiufan's vanguard had already arrived at Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng reached Xinting, but before the defenses were complete—on xīnmǎo—Xiufan's vanguard was already at Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 道成方解衣高臥以安眾心，徐索白虎幡，登西垣，使寧朔將軍高道慶、羽林監陳顯達、員外郎王敬則帥舟師與休范戰，頗有殺獲。

translations.literal: Daocheng was just then loosening his clothes and lying down at ease to calm the troops' hearts; he slowly asked for the White Tiger banner, ascended the western rampart, and had General of Pacifying the North Gao Daoqing, Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers Chen Xianda, and Supernumerary Gentleman Wang Jingze lead the river fleet to fight Xiufan, with considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng was at that moment loosening his garments and reclining at ease to steady the troops; slowly he sent for the White Tiger banner, climbed the western rampart, and ordered Gao Daoqing, General of Pacifying the North, Chen Xianda, Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers, and Wang Jingze, Supernumerary Gentleman, to lead the river fleet against Xiufan, inflicting considerable casualties.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，休范自新林捨舟步上，其將丁文豪請休范直攻台城。

translations.literal: On the day rénchén, Xiufan left his boats at Xinlin and advanced on foot; his general Ding Wenhao urged Xiufan to strike the capital directly.
translations.idiomatic: On rénchén Xiufan abandoned his boats at Xinlin and marched on foot; his general Ding Wenhao urged him to strike the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 休范遣文豪別將兵趣台城，自以大眾攻新亭壘。

translations.literal: Xiufan sent Wenhao with a separate force toward the capital while he himself led the main army against the Xinting fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan sent Wenhao with a detached force toward the capital while he himself led the main army against the Xinting fortifications.

sentences.zh: 道成帥將士悉力拒戰，自巳至午，外勢愈盛，眾皆失色，道成曰：「賊雖多而亂，尋當破矣。」

translations.literal: Daocheng led his officers and men to resist with all their strength; from the si hour to the wu hour the enemy pressure grew ever fiercer and all turned pale. Daocheng said: "Though many, the rebels are disorderly—they will soon be broken."
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng led his officers and men to resist with all their strength; from the si hour to the wu hour the enemy pressure mounted and faces paled. Daocheng said: "They are many but disorderly—the rebels will soon be broken.”

sentences.zh: 休范白服，乘肩輿，自登城南臨滄觀，以數十人自衛。

translations.literal: Xiufan wore white robes, rode in a shoulder-borne palanquin, and himself ascended the watchtower facing Cang on the south wall, with only a few dozen men for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan wore white robes, rode in a shoulder-borne palanquin, and climbed the watchtower facing Cang on the south wall, guarded by only a few dozen men.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉黃回與越騎校尉張敬兒謀詐降以取之。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Handlers of Tributary Cavalry Huang Hui and Commandant of the Yue Cavalry Zhang Jing'er plotted to feign surrender and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, Commandant of the Handlers of Tributary Cavalry, and Zhang Jing'er, Commandant of the Yue Cavalry, plotted to feign surrender and seize him.

sentences.zh: 回謂敬兒曰：「卿可取之，我誓不殺諸王！」

translations.literal: Hui said to Jing'er: "You may take him—I swear I will not kill any prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said to Jing'er: "You take him—I swear I will not kill any prince!"

sentences.zh: 敬兒以白道成。

translations.literal: Jing'er reported this to Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er brought word of this to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成曰：「卿能力事，當以本州相賞。」

translations.literal: Daocheng said: "If you can accomplish this, I shall reward you with your native province."
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng said: "If you can carry this off, I will reward you with your native province."

sentences.zh: 乃與回出城南，放仗走，大呼稱降。

translations.literal: They then went out beyond the south gate together, cast aside their weapons and fled, shouting that they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Together they passed beyond the south gate, cast down their weapons, and fled, shouting that they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 休范喜，召至輿側，回陽致道成密意，休范信之，以二子德宣、德嗣付道成為質。

translations.literal: Xiufan rejoiced, summoned them to his palanquin; Hui pretended to convey Daocheng's secret intentions; Xiufan believed him and entrusted his two sons Dexuan and Dexi to Daocheng as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan was delighted and summoned them beside his palanquin; Hui pretended to convey Daocheng's secret intentions; Xiufan believed him and sent his two sons Dexuan and Dexi to Daocheng as hostages.

sentences.zh: 二子至，道成即斬之。

translations.literal: When the two sons arrived, Daocheng immediately had them executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the two sons arrived, Daocheng had them executed at once.

sentences.zh: 休范置回、敬兒於左右，所親李恆、鐘爽諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Xiufan kept Hui and Jing'er at his side; his close associates Li Heng and Zhong Shuang remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan kept Hui and Jing'er close at hand; his intimates Li Heng and Zhong Shuang remonstrated with him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時休范日飲醇酒，回見休范無備，目敬兒；

translations.literal: By then Xiufan was drinking heavily every day; Hui saw that Xiufan was off guard and signaled Jing'er with a look;
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiufan was drinking heavily every day; Hui saw that he was off guard and signaled Jing'er with a glance;

sentences.zh: 敬兒奪休范防身刀，斬休范首，左右皆散走。

translations.literal: Jing'er seized Xiufan's personal dagger and cut off Xiufan's head; those at his side all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er snatched Xiufan's personal dagger and struck off his head; those standing about him all fled.

sentences.zh: 敬兒馳馬持首歸新亭。

translations.literal: Jing'er galloped back to Xinting holding the head.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er galloped back to Xinting, the head in his hand.

sentences.zh: 道成遣隊主陳靈寶送休范首還台。

translations.literal: Daocheng sent Squad Commander Chen Lingbao to carry Xiufan's head back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng dispatched Squad Commander Chen Lingbao to carry Xiufan's head back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 靈寶道逢休范兵，棄首於水，挺身得達，唱云「已平」，而無以為驗，眾莫之信。

translations.literal: Chen Lingbao encountered Xiufan's troops on the road, threw the head into the water, and broke through alone; he cried out, "All is pacified," but having nothing to prove it, no one believed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Chen Lingbao ran into Xiufan's troops; he cast the head into the water and broke through alone, crying, "All is pacified!"—but with nothing to show for it, no one believed him.

sentences.zh: 休范將士亦不之知，其將杜黑騾攻新亭甚急。

translations.literal: Xiufan's officers and soldiers also did not know it; his general Du Heiluan pressed the attack on Xinting very fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan's troops likewise had no word of it; his general Du Heiluan was pressing the assault on Xinting with great fury.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成在射堂，司空主簿蕭惠朗帥敢死士數十人突入東門，至射堂下。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng was at the archery hall; Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works Xiao Huilang led several dozen dare-to-die troops in a sudden entry through the east gate, reaching below the archery hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng was at the archery hall when Xiao Huilang, chief clerk to the Minister of Works, led several dozen dare-to-die troops in a surprise rush through the east gate to the foot of the hall.

sentences.zh: 道成上馬，帥麾下搏戰，惠朗乃退，道成復得保城。

translations.literal: Daocheng mounted his horse, led his subordinates in close combat, Huilang then withdrew, and Daocheng again was able to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng mounted and led his men in hand-to-hand fighting; Huilang fell back, and Daocheng held the city once more.

sentences.zh: 惠朗，惠開之弟也，其姊為休范妃。

translations.literal: Huilang was Huikai's younger brother; his elder sister was Xiufan's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Huilang was the younger brother of Huikai; his elder sister was married to Xiufan.

sentences.zh: 惠朗兄黃門郎惠明，明為道成軍副，在城內，了不自疑。

translations.literal: Huilang's elder brother, Gentlemen-at-the-Palace Gates Huiming—Ming serving as Daocheng's army deputy, was inside the city and wholly did not suspect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huilang's elder brother Huiming, a Gentlemen-at-the-Palace Gates who served as Daocheng's deputy commander, was inside the city and never suspected himself at all.

sentences.zh: 道成與黑騾拒戰，自晡達旦，矢石不息；

translations.literal: Daocheng and Heiluan resisted in battle; from the shen hour until dawn, arrows and stones did not cease;
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng battled Heiluan from dusk until dawn without a pause in the hail of arrows and stones;

sentences.zh: 其夜，大雨，鼓叫不復相聞。

translations.literal: That night, heavy rain fell; drums and shouting could no longer be heard by one another.
translations.idiomatic: That night a torrential rain fell, and drumbeats and battle cries could no longer be heard above the storm.

sentences.zh: 將士積日不得寢食，軍中馬夜驚，城內亂走。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers for days on end could not sleep or eat; in the army horses startled at night, and inside the city men ran about in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had gone days without sleep or food; horses panicked in the night, and men ran wildly through the city.

sentences.zh: 道成秉燭正坐，厲聲呵之，如是者數四。

translations.literal: Daocheng held a candle and sat upright, shouting at them sternly—thus four or five times.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng sat upright by candlelight and shouted them down sternly, doing so again and again.

sentences.zh: 丁文豪破台軍於皁莢橋，直至朱雀桁南，杜黑騾亦捨新亭北趣朱雀桁。

translations.literal: Ding Wenhao broke the capital army at Zaoji Bridge, advancing straight to south of the Vermilion Bird pontoon; Du Heiluan also abandoned Xinting and hurried north toward the Vermilion Bird pontoon.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wenhao routed the capital's forces at Zaoji Bridge and pushed all the way to the south end of the Vermilion Bird pontoon; Du Heiluan likewise abandoned Xinting and raced north toward the same bridge.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍王道隆將羽林精兵在朱雀門內，急召鄱陽忠昭公劉勉於石頭。

translations.literal: General of the Right Army Wang Daolong led elite Feathered Forest troops inside the Vermilion Bird Gate, urgently summoning Liu Mian, Duke of Poyang and bearer of the title Loyal and Illustrious, at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Daolong, General of the Right Army, held elite Feathered Forest troops inside the Vermilion Bird Gate and urgently summoned Liu Mian, the Loyal and Illustrious Duke of Poyang, at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 勉至，命撤桁以折南軍之勢，道隆怒曰：「賊至，但當急擊，寧可開桁自弱邪！」

translations.literal: When Mian arrived, he ordered the pontoon dismantled to break the southern army's momentum; Daolong angrily said: "The rebels have come—one should only strike them urgently; how can one open the pontoon and weaken oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: When Mian arrived, he ordered the pontoon taken up to check the southern army's momentum. Daolong snapped: "The enemy is here—we should hit them hard. Why dismantle the bridge and weaken ourselves!"

sentences.zh: 勉不敢復言。

translations.literal: Mian did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 道隆趣勉進戰，勉渡桁南，戰敗而死。

translations.literal: Daolong urged Mian forward to battle; Mian crossed south of the pontoon, was defeated in battle, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong pressed Mian to attack; Mian crossed to the south side of the pontoon, was defeated, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 黑騾等乘勝渡淮，道隆棄眾走還台，黑騾兵追殺之。

translations.literal: Heiluan and the rest, riding victory, crossed the Huai; Daolong abandoned the multitude and fled back to the capital; Heiluan's troops pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Heiluan and his men crossed the Huai in pursuit of victory; Daolong abandoned his troops and fled back toward the capital, and Heiluan's soldiers ran him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎王蘊重傷，踣於御溝之側，或扶之以免。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Wang Yun was heavily wounded, collapsed beside the imperial moat; someone supported him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, was gravely wounded and fell beside the imperial moat; someone pulled him aside, and he survived.

sentences.zh: 蘊，景文之兄子也。

translations.literal: Yun was Jingwen's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was the nephew of Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 於是中外大震，道路皆云「台城已陷」，白下、石頭之眾皆潰，張永、沈懷明逃還。

translations.literal: Thereupon court and countryside were greatly shaken; on the roads all said "The capital has fallen"; the forces at Baixia and Shitou all scattered; Zhang Yong and Shen Huaiming fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept court and countryside; travelers everywhere said, "The capital has fallen"; the garrisons at Baixia and Shitou broke and fled; Zhang Yong and Shen Huaiming retreated in disorder.

sentences.zh: 宮中傳新亭亦陷，太后執帝手泣曰：「天下敗矣！」

translations.literal: Within the palace came word that Xinting too had fallen; the empress dowager grasped the emperor's hand and wept, saying: "The realm is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: Word reached the palace that Xinting too had fallen. The empress dowager took the emperor's hand and wept: "The realm is lost!”

sentences.zh: 先是，月犯右執法，太白犯上將，或勸劉勉解職。

translations.literal: Earlier, the moon invaded the Right Enforcer, and the Metal Star invaded the Senior General; some urged Liu Mian to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the moon had trespassed on the Right Enforcer, and Venus had trespassed on the Senior General; some urged Liu Mian to give up his office.

sentences.zh: 勉曰：「吾執心行己，無愧幽明，若災眚必至，避豈得免！」

translations.literal: Mian said: "I hold my heart and conduct myself—without shame before the hidden or the manifest; if calamity must come, can avoidance obtain escape!"
translations.idiomatic: Mian said: "I conduct myself by my own conscience and have nothing to hide before heaven or earth. If disaster is fated, how can fleeing save me?"

sentences.zh: 勉晚年頗慕高尚，立園宅，名為東山，遺落世務，罷遣部曲。

translations.literal: In his later years Mian was much drawn to lofty reclusion; he established an estate and named it Eastern Hill, neglected worldly affairs, and dismissed his personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Mian had grown enamored of a lofty, secluded life. He built an estate he called Eastern Hill, withdrew from public affairs, and disbanded his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成謂勉曰：「將軍受顧命，輔幼主，當此艱難之日，而深尚從容，廢省羽翼。

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng said to Mian: "The general received the late emperor's charge to assist the young ruler; on this difficult day you yet deeply esteem leisurely ease and have reduced and dismissed your wings and talons.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng told Mian: "You were entrusted with the regency to guide a young emperor. In these desperate days you have grown fond of leisure and stripped away your own strength.

sentences.zh: 一朝事至，悔可追乎！」

translations.literal: When crisis arrives in a morning, can regret be pursued and retrieved!"
translations.idiomatic: When crisis strikes, will regret help you then?"

sentences.zh: 勉不從而敗。

translations.literal: Mian did not follow his advice and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Mian refused to listen—and paid for it with defeat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，撫軍長史褚澄開東府門納南軍，擁安成王准據東府，稱桂陽王教曰：「安成王，吾子也，勿得侵犯。」

translations.literal: On day jiawu, Adjutant to the Pacifying General Chu Cheng opened the Eastern Palace gate and admitted the southern army, supporting Prince of Ancheng Zhun in holding the Eastern Palace, proclaiming in the name of the Prince of Guiyang a command: "The Prince of Ancheng is my son—do not encroach upon him."
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu, Chu Cheng, adjutant to the Pacifying General, opened the Eastern Palace gate to the southern army. He installed Prince Zhun of Ancheng in the palace and issued a proclamation in the Prince of Guiyang's name: "The Prince of Ancheng is my son—do not harm him."

sentences.zh: 澄，淵之弟也。

translations.literal: Cheng was Yuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was the younger brother of Chu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 杜黑騾徑進至杜姥宅，中書舍人孫千齡開承明門出降，宮省恇憂。

translations.literal: Du Heiluan pressed straight forward to the Old Du's residence; Palace Secretary Attendant Sun Qianling opened the Chenming Gate and went out to surrender; the palace and ministries were frightened and anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Du Heiluan marched straight to the Old Du's residence; Sun Qianling, a Palace Secretary Attendant, opened the Chenming Gate and surrendered; the palace and ministries were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 時府藏已竭，皇太后、太妃剔取宮中金銀器物以充賞，眾莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: At the time the treasury stores were already exhausted; the empress dowager and imperial consort picked out gold and silver utensils from the palace to serve as rewards, but the multitude had no fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: By then the treasury was empty; the empress dowager and the imperial consort stripped gold and silver from the palace to pay the troops, but no one had the heart to fight.

sentences.zh: 俄而丁文豪之從知休范已死，稍欲退散。

translations.literal: Before long, Ding Wenhao's followers learned that Xiufan was already dead and gradually wished to disperse and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wenhao's followers learned that Xiufan was dead and began to melt away.

sentences.zh: 文豪厲聲曰：「我獨不能定天下邪！」

translations.literal: Wenhao said in a stern voice: "Can I alone not settle the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenhao shouted: "Am I not enough to settle the realm myself!"

sentences.zh: 許公輿詐稱桂陽王在新亭，士民惶惑，詣蕭道成壘投刺者以千數。

translations.literal: Xu Gongyu falsely claimed the Prince of Guiyang was at Xinting; officials and common people were frightened and confused; those who went to Xiao Daocheng's camp to submit name cards numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Gongyu spread the false report that the Prince of Guiyang was still at Xinting. Terrified townspeople flocked by the thousands to Xiao Daocheng's camp to surrender their name cards.

sentences.zh: 道成得，皆焚之，登北城謂曰；

translations.literal: Daocheng received them and burned them all, ascended the north wall, and addressed them:
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng collected the cards, burned them all, climbed the north wall, and called out:

sentences.zh: 「劉休范父子昨已就戮，屍在南岡下。

translations.literal: "Father and son Liu Xiufan were executed yesterday; their corpses are below the southern ridge.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Xiufan and his sons were executed yesterday. Their bodies lie below the southern ridge.

sentences.zh: 身是蕭平南，諸君諦視之，名刺皆已焚，勿憂懼也。」

translations.literal: I am Xiao Pingnan—look at me carefully; the name cards have all been burned; do not worry or fear."
translations.idiomatic: I am Xiao Pingnan—look closely. Your name cards are already ash. Have no fear.”

sentences.zh: 道成遣陳顯達、張敬兒及輔師將軍任農夫、馬軍主東平周盤龍等將兵，自石頭濟淮，從承明門入衛宮省。

translations.literal: Daocheng dispatched Chen Xianda, Zhang Jing'er, and Auxiliary Commander Ren Nongfu, Cavalry Commander Zhou Panlong of Dongping, and others to lead troops; they crossed the Huai from Shitou and entered through the Chenming Gate to guard the palace and ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng sent Chen Xianda, Zhang Jing'er, Auxiliary Commander Ren Nongfu, and Cavalry Commander Zhou Panlong of Dongping with their troops across the Huai from Shitou; they entered through the Chenming Gate to defend the palace.

sentences.zh: 袁粲慷慨謂諸將曰：「今寇賊已逼而眾情離沮，孤子受先帝付託，不能綏靖國家，請與諸君同死社稷！」

translations.literal: Yuan Can spoke with noble fervor to the generals: "Now the bandits and rebels have already pressed close while the multitude's sentiment is scattered and disheartened; this orphaned son received the former emperor's entrustment and cannot pacify and settle the state—please let me die with you all for the altars of soil and grain!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can addressed the generals with burning resolve: "The enemy is at the gates and morale is collapsing. I was charged by the late emperor to steady the realm and have failed. Let us die together for the state!"

sentences.zh: 被甲上馬，將驅之。

translations.literal: He donned armor, mounted his horse, and was about to drive them forward.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor, mounted, and prepared to lead them out.

sentences.zh: 於是陳顯達等引兵出戰，大破杜黑騾於杜姥宅，飛矢貫達目。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chen Xianda and the rest led troops out to battle and greatly defeated Du Heiluan at the Old Du's residence; a flying arrow pierced through Da's eye.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda and his men marched out and routed Du Heiluan at the Old Du's residence. A stray arrow pierced Xianda's eye.

sentences.zh: 丙申，張敬兒等又破黑騾等於宣陽門，斬黑騾及丁文豪，進克東府，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Zhang Jing'er and the rest again defeated Heiluan and the rest at the Xuanyang Gate, beheaded Heiluan and Ding Wenhao, advanced and seized the Eastern Palace, and all remaining partisans were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen, Zhang Jing'er broke Heiluan's forces again at the Xuanyang Gate, beheaded Heiluan and Ding Wenhao, took the Eastern Palace, and wiped out the last of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成振旅還建康，百姓緣道聚觀，曰：「全國家者，此公也！」

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng returned his troops in good order to Jiankang; common people lined the road to gather and watch, saying: "The one who saved the state and house is this lord!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng marched his troops back into Jiankang in good order. People lined the roads crying: "This is the man who saved the realm!"

sentences.zh: 道成與袁粲、褚淵、劉秉皆上表引咎解職，不許。

translations.literal: Daocheng, together with Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing, all submitted memorials accepting blame and seeking to resign their posts—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng, Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing all memorialized the throne accepting blame and offering to resign—but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，解嚴，大赦。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, the emergency curfew was lifted and a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, martial law ended and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 柔然遣使來聘。

translations.literal: Rouran sent envoys on a court visit.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran sent envoys to pay a formal visit to the court.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚子，以平南將軍蕭道成為中領軍、南兗州刺史，留衛建康，與袁粲、褚淵、劉秉更日入直決事，號為「四貴」。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day gengzi: the General Who Pacifies the South Xiao Daocheng was made Central Army Inspector and Governor of South Yanzhou, remaining to guard Jiankang; with Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing he entered duty on rotation to decide affairs, and they were called the "Four Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day gengzi, Xiao Daocheng, General Who Pacifies the South, was appointed Central Army Inspector and Governor of South Yanzhou and left at Jiankang to guard the capital. He joined Yuan Can, Chu Yuan, and Liu Bing in rotating daily duty at court, and together they were known as the "Four Nobles."

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休范之反也，使道士陳公昭作《天公書》，題云「沈丞相」，付荊州刺史沈攸之門者。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guiyang Xiufan rebelled, he had the Daoist Chen Gongzhao compose a "Heavenly Lord's Letter," inscribed with the words "Chancellor Shen," and delivered it to the doorkeeper of Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiufan's revolt, he had the Daoist Chen Gongzhao write a "Letter from the Heavenly Lord" addressed to "Chancellor Shen" and deliver it to the gate of Jingzhou governor Shen Youzhi.

sentences.zh: 攸之不開視，推得公昭，送之朝廷。

translations.literal: Youzhi did not open and read it; through investigation he obtained Gongzhao and sent him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi never opened the document; he tracked down Gongzhao and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及休范反，攸之謂僚佐曰：「杜陽必聲言我與之同。

translations.literal: When Xiufan rebelled, Youzhi said to his staff: "Du Yang will surely proclaim that I am together with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiufan rose in rebellion, Youzhi told his staff: "Du Yang will surely claim I sided with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 若不顛沛勤王，必增朝野之惑。」

translations.literal: If I do not toil in distress to serve the ruler zealously, I shall surely increase the court and countryside's bewilderment."
translations.idiomatic: Unless I rush to the emperor's aid in disarray, court and countryside will only grow more confused."

sentences.zh: 乃與南徐州刺史建平王景素、郢州刺史晉熙王燮、湘州刺史王僧虔、雍州刺史張興世同舉兵討休范。

translations.literal: He then, together with South Xuzhou Inspector Prince of Jianping Jingsu, Yingzhou Inspector Prince of Jinxi Xie, Xiangzhou Inspector Wang Sengqian, and Yongzhou Inspector Zhang Xingshi, jointly raised troops to punish Xiufan.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined South Xuzhou governor Prince Jingsu of Jianping, Yingzhou governor Prince Xie of Jinxi, Xiangzhou governor Wang Sengqian, and Yongzhou governor Zhang Xingshi in raising armies against Xiufan.

sentences.zh: 休范留中兵參軍長惠連等守尋陽，燮遣中兵參軍馮景祖襲之。

translations.literal: Xiufan left Middle Army Administrator Zhang Huilian and others to hold Xunyang; Xie sent Middle Army Administrator Feng Jingzu to raid them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiufan left Middle Army Administrator Zhang Huilian and others to garrison Xunyang; Xie sent Middle Army Administrator Feng Jingzu to attack them.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，惠連等開門請降，殺休范二子，諸鎮皆罷兵。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Huilian and the rest opened the gate and requested surrender; Xiufan's two sons were killed, and all garrison commands ceased their troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Huilian opened the gates and surrendered. Xiufan's two sons were executed, and the regional commands all stood down.

sentences.zh: 景素，宏之子也。

translations.literal: Jingsu was Hong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu was the son of Hong.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏詔曰：「下民凶戾，不顧親戚，一人為惡，殃及闔門。

translations.literal: On day yimao, Wei issued an edict: "The lower people are fierce and perverse, heedless of kin; when one person does evil, calamity reaches the whole gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yimao, Northern Wei issued an edict: "Common folk have grown cruel and reckless, kinship be damned. When one man turns wicked, his whole household pays.

sentences.zh: 朕為民父母，深所愍悼。

translations.literal: We as parents of the people deeply commiserate and mourn.
translations.idiomatic: As father and mother to the people, We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 自今非謀反、大逆、外叛，罪止其身。」

translations.literal: From now on, for crimes other than plotting rebellion, great treason, or external defection, guilt stops with the person himself."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, except for plotting rebellion, great treason, or defecting to a foreign state, punishment shall fall on the offender alone."

sentences.zh: 於是始罷門、房之誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon was begun the abolition of clan- and household-extinction punishments.
translations.idiomatic: With this, Wei abolished punishments that wiped out whole clans and household branches.

sentences.zh: 魏顯祖勤於為治，賞罰嚴明，慎擇牧守，進廉退貪。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Xianzu was diligent in governing; rewards and punishments were strict and clear; he carefully chose pasture and garrison officials, advancing the incorrupt and dismissing the greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu of Wei was a tireless administrator: rewards and punishments were exact, provincial appointments carefully chosen, the honest promoted and the corrupt removed.

sentences.zh: 諸曹疑事，舊多奏決，又口傳詔敕，或致矯擅。

translations.literal: In the various bureaus, doubtful matters in the old way were mostly decided by memorial; moreover oral transmission of edicts and commands sometimes led to wrongful usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old ways, doubtful cases in the ministries were often settled by memorial, and oral orders from the throne could be forged or abused.

sentences.zh: 上皇命事無大小，皆據律正名，不得為疑奏；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor ordered that matters great and small all be according to law given correct names, and memorials of doubt were not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor ruled that every case, great or small, must be decided strictly by law—no more "doubtful matter" memorials;

sentences.zh: 合則制可，違則彈詰，盡用墨詔，由是事皆精審。

translations.literal: if compliant then approved, if in violation then impeached and interrogated; all used ink edicts—thereby affairs all became finely examined.
translations.idiomatic: lawful rulings were approved, unlawful ones challenged; every order went out in written edict, and justice became meticulous.

sentences.zh: 尤重刑罰，大刑多令覆鞫，或囚系積年。

translations.literal: He especially emphasized punishments; for major penalties he often ordered re-examination, and sometimes prisoners were detained for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially severe on punishment: major sentences were often reviewed again and again, and prisoners sometimes languished for years.

sentences.zh: 群臣頗以為言，上皇曰：「滯獄誠非善治，不猶俞於侖猝而濫乎！

translations.literal: The various ministers spoke of this considerably; the Retired Emperor said: "Delayed cases are truly not good governance—are they not still better than sudden and excessive rushing!
translations.idiomatic: Ministers complained, but the retired emperor replied: "Backlogged cases are poor government—but are they not better than rushed and sloppy justice?

sentences.zh: 夫人幽苦則思善，故智者以囹圄為福堂，朕特苦之，欲其改悔而加矜恕爾。」

translations.literal: When people are in dark suffering they then think of goodness; therefore the wise take the prison as a hall of blessing—we specially make them suffer, wishing them to reform and repent and thereby increase clemency and forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: Hardship turns the mind toward goodness; the wise call prison a hall of blessing. We make prisoners suffer deliberately so they will repent—and so We may show mercy."

sentences.zh: 由是囚系雖滯，而所刑多得其宜。

translations.literal: Thereby, though imprisonments were delayed, the punishments applied mostly attained their proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisonment dragged on, but the punishments handed down were mostly just.

sentences.zh: 又以赦令長奸，故自延興以後，不復有赦。

translations.literal: Moreover, because amnesty edicts nourished wickedness, from Yansing onward there were no longer amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: He also believed amnesties encouraged crime, so after the Yansing era there were no more general pardons.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚辰，立皇弟友為邵陵王。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gengchen: the emperor's younger brother You was established as Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day gengchen, the emperor's younger brother You was created Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，加荊州刺史沈攸之開府儀同三司，攸之固辭。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi was advanced to Grand Master with Honors Equal to the Three Dukes; Youzhi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Jingzhou governor Shen Youzhi was granted honorary status equal to the Three Dukes; Youzhi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 執政欲征攸之而憚於發命，乃以太后令遣中使謂曰：「公久勞於外，宜還京師。

translations.literal: The regents wished to summon Youzhi but feared issuing the command; they therefore used an empress dowager order to send a palace envoy to say: "The duke has long toiled outside—he ought to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The regents wanted to recall Youzhi but hesitated to issue the order directly, so they sent a palace envoy with an empress dowager's command: "You have borne the burden abroad too long. It is time to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 任寄實重，未欲輕之；

translations.literal: The charge entrusted is truly weighty—we do not yet wish to treat it lightly;
translations.idiomatic: Your post is vital, and We do not take it lightly;

sentences.zh: 進退可否，在公所擇。」

translations.literal: advancing or retiring, approving or declining—all lies in what the duke chooses."
translations.idiomatic: whether you come or stay is for you to decide."

sentences.zh: 攸之曰：「臣無廓廟之資，居中實非其才。

translations.literal: Youzhi said: "Your subject has no material for the grand temple; occupying the center is truly not his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi replied: "I lack the talents of a statesman. I am not cut out for court.

sentences.zh: 至於撲討蠻、蜑，克清江、漢，不敢有辭。

translations.literal: As for beating down and subduing the Man and Dan tribes, conquering and clearing the Jiang and Han—your subject does not dare have any demurral.
translations.idiomatic: But when it comes to crushing the Man and Dan barbarians and pacifying the Jiang and Han, I ask for no exemption.

sentences.zh: 雖自上如此，去留伏聽朝旨。」

translations.literal: Though from above it is thus, in going or staying your subject listens humbly to the court's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Even so, whether I stay or go is entirely for the court to command."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，柔然寇魏敦煌，尉多侯擊破之。

translations.literal: On day guisi, Rouran raided Wei's Dunhuang; Wei Duohou defeated and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Rouran raided Dunhuang in Wei territory; Wei Duohou drove them off.

sentences.zh: 尚書秦：「敦煌僻遠，介居西、北強寇之間，恐不能自固，請內徙就涼州。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat submitted: "Dunhuang is remote and isolated, situated between strong bandits of west and north—we fear it cannot secure itself; we request internal relocation to draw near Liangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat memorialized: "Dunhuang is remote and sits between powerful enemies to the west and north. We fear it cannot hold. We ask that it be moved inland toward Liangzhou."

sentences.zh: 群臣集議，皆以為然。

translations.literal: The various ministers gathered in council and all considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers debated the proposal and all agreed.

sentences.zh: 給事中昌黎韓秀獨以為：「敦煌之置，為日已久。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Han Xiu of Changli alone considered: "Dunhuang's establishment has had days already long.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Han Xiu of Changli alone dissented: "Dunhuang has been a garrison for generations.

sentences.zh: 雖逼強寇，人習戰鬥，縱有草竊，不為大害。

translations.literal: Though pressed by strong bandits, the people are practiced in battle; even if there are grass-bandit pilferings, it is not a great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Though menaced by strong enemies, the people there are hardened fighters. Petty raids are no serious threat.

sentences.zh: 循常置戍，足以自全；

translations.literal: Following routine in posting garrisons is sufficient to secure oneself;
translations.idiomatic: Routine garrisons are enough to keep it safe;

sentences.zh: 而能隔閡西、北二虜，使不得相通。

translations.literal: and it can block and separate the two barbarians of west and north, causing them not to be able to communicate with each other.
translations.idiomatic: and it blocks the western and northern barbarians from joining forces.

sentences.zh: 今徙就涼州，不唯有蹙國之名，且姑臧去敦煌千有餘里，防邏甚難，二虜必有交通闚□之志；

translations.literal: Now in relocating to draw near Liangzhou, not only is there a name of shrinking the state; moreover Guzang is more than a thousand li from Dunhuang—border patrol is very difficult—the two barbarians will surely have designs of communicating and [?] together;
translations.idiomatic: Moving it toward Liangzhou would not only shrink the realm in name; Guzang lies more than a thousand li from Dunhuang, making defense nearly impossible—and the two barbarian powers would surely seize the chance to link up and scheme together;

sentences.zh: 若騷動涼州，則關中不得安枕。

translations.literal: if Liangzhou is disturbed and shaken, then within the passes one cannot rest one's head on a pillow.
translations.idiomatic: If Liangzhou were thrown into turmoil, no one in Guanzhong could sleep easy.

sentences.zh: 又，士民或安土重遷，招引外寇，為國深患，不可不慮也。」

translations.literal: Further, officials and people may feel at peace in their native soil and be heavy to relocate, inviting and drawing in external bandits—becoming a deep peril to the state; this cannot go unconsidered."
translations.idiomatic: And locals who dread leaving their homes might invite outside raiders in—a grave danger the court must weigh."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁酉，以尚書令袁粲為中書監、領司徒；

translations.literal: Ninth month, day dingyou: Secretarial Director Yuan Can was made Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day dingyou, Yuan Can, Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 加褚淵尚書令；

translations.literal: Chu Yuan was advanced to Secretarial Director;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan was promoted to Director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 劉秉丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Liu Bing was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing was made governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 粲固辭，求反居墓所；

translations.literal: Can firmly declined, requesting to return and dwell at his ancestral tomb site;
translations.idiomatic: Can firmly declined and asked to retire to his family graves;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 淵以褚澄為吳郡太守，司徒左長史蕭惠明言於朝曰：「褚澄開門納賊，更為股肱大郡，王蘊力戰幾死，棄而不收。

translations.literal: Yuan made Chu Cheng Governor of Wu Commandery; Left Senior Administrator to the Minister of Works Xiao Huiming spoke at court: "Chu Cheng opened the gate and admitted rebels, yet is again made a great commandery of arm and thigh; Wang Yun fought fiercely nearly to death, yet was cast aside and not taken back in.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan appointed Chu Cheng governor of Wu Commandery. Xiao Huiming, left senior administrator to the Minister of Works, protested at court: "Chu Cheng opened the gates to the rebels, yet wins a major commandery. Wang Yun nearly died fighting for the realm and is cast aside.

sentences.zh: 賞罰如此，何憂不亂！」

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments thus—what worry is there of not having disorder!"
translations.idiomatic: With rewards and punishments like these, how can order fail to collapse!"

sentences.zh: 淵甚慚。

translations.literal: Yuan was very ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan was deeply shamed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚申，以侍中王蘊為湘州刺史。
