translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yun was made Xiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengshen, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yun was appointed governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，帝加元服，大赦。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingxu: the emperor was invested with the cap of adulthood; general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day bingxu, the emperor came of age and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸亥，立皇弟躋為江夏王，贊為武陵王。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day guihai: the emperor's younger brothers Ji was established as Prince of Jiangxia, and Zan as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day guihai, the emperor's younger brothers Ji and Zan were created Princes of Jiangxia and Wuling, respectively.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏建安貞王陸□卒。

translations.literal: This year, Wei's Prince of Jian'an and Zhen, Lu [?], died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lu [?], Prince of Jian'an and Zhen in Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝下元徽三年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the annals of Emperor Ming Taizong, third year of Yuanhui (
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of the reign of Emperor Ming Taizong, third year of Yuanhui (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元四七五年）

translations.literal: yǐmǎo, corresponding to the year 475 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yǐmǎo [sexagenary year], AD 475)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，帝祀南郊、明堂。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day xīnsì: the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and the Hall of Illumination.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day xīnsì [29 January 475], the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar and the Hall of Illumination.

sentences.zh: 蕭道成以襄陽重鎮，張敬兒人位俱輕，不欲使居之；

translations.literal: Xiao Daocheng, because Xiangyang was a vital stronghold and Zhang Jinger's person and position were both light, did not wish him to hold it;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Daocheng considered Xiangyang a vital stronghold and thought Zhang Jinger too slight in stature and rank to hold it;

sentences.zh: 而敬兒求之不已，謂道成曰：「沈攸之在荊州，公知其欲何所作；

translations.literal: yet Jinger begged for it without cease and said to Daocheng, "Shen Youzhi is in Jingzhou—you know what he intends to do;
translations.idiomatic: but Jinger kept pressing for the post and told Daocheng, "Shen Youzhi is in Jingzhou—you know what he is plotting;

sentences.zh: 不出敬兒，以表裡制之，恐非公之利。」

translations.literal: if you do not send out Jinger to control him inside and out, I fear it will not be to your advantage."
translations.idiomatic: if you do not post me there to control him from within and without, I fear it will not serve your interests."

sentences.zh: 道成笑而無言。

translations.literal: Daocheng smiled and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 三月，己巳，以驍騎將軍張敬兒為都督雍、梁二州諸軍事、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, day jǐsì: Zhang Jinger, General of the Valiant Cavalry, was made commander of all military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces and governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jǐsì [24 March 475], Zhang Jinger, General of the Valiant Cavalry, was appointed commander of Yong and Liang military affairs and governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之聞敬兒上，恐其見襲，陰為之備。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi heard that Jinger had been promoted, he feared an attack and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi learned of Jinger's appointment, he feared an attack and secretly prepared his defenses.

sentences.zh: 敬兒既至，奉事攸之，親敬甚至，動輒咨稟，信饋不絕。

translations.literal: When Jinger arrived, he served Youzhi with utmost respect and intimacy, consulting and reporting on every matter, letters and gifts unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinger arrived, he served Youzhi with elaborate respect, consulting him on every matter and sending an unbroken stream of letters and gifts.

sentences.zh: 攸之以為誠然，酬報款厚。

translations.literal: Youzhi believed this sincere and responded with warm and generous returns.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi took this for genuine loyalty and responded with warm, generous courtesies.

sentences.zh: 累書欲因遊獵會境上，敬兒報以為：「心期有在，景跡不宜過敦。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly wrote wishing to meet on the border during a hunting excursion; Jinger replied that "our hearts are pledged, but appearances should not be made too intimate."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly proposed meeting on the border during a hunt; Jinger replied that "our hearts are pledged, but we should not make our dealings look too intimate."

sentences.zh: 攸之益信之。

translations.literal: Youzhi trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 敬兒得其事跡，皆密白道成。

translations.literal: Jinger obtained intelligence on his activities and reported it all in secret to Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger gathered intelligence on his activities and reported everything in secret to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成與攸之書，問：「張雍州遷代之日，將欲誰擬？」

translations.literal: Daocheng wrote to Youzhi asking, "When Zhang of Yongzhou is transferred, whom do you intend to nominate?"
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng wrote to Youzhi asking, "When Zhang of Yongzhou is transferred, whom do you plan to nominate as his successor?"

sentences.zh: 攸之即以示敬兒，欲以間之。

translations.literal: Youzhi at once showed this to Jinger, intending to sow discord between them.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi immediately showed the letter to Jinger, hoping to drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙午，魏主使員外散騎常侍許赤虎來聘。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day bǐngwǔ: the Wei emperor sent Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry Xu Chihu on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on the day bǐngwǔ [20 May 475], the Northern Wei emperor sent Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu Chihu on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主如武州山；

translations.literal: On day dīngwèi the Wei emperor went to Wuzhou Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dīngwèi [21 May 475] the Northern Wei emperor went to Wuzhou Mountain;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，如車輪山。

translations.literal: on day xīyǒu he went to Chelun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: on the day xīyǒu [4 June 475] he went to Chelun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚午，魏初禁殺牛馬。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day gēngwǔ: Wei for the first time forbade the killing of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day gēngwǔ [13 June 475], Northern Wei for the first time forbade the slaughter of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 袁粲、褚淵皆固讓新官。

translations.literal: Yuan Can and Chu Yuan both firmly declined their new offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and Chu Yuan both firmly declined their new appointments.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚戌，復以粲為尚書令，八月，庚子，加護軍將軍褚淵中書監。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day gēngxū: Can was again made Director of the Secretariat; eighth month, day gēngzǐ: Protector-General Chu Yuan was given the additional post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day gēngxū [11 August 475], Can was again appointed Director of the Secretariat; in the eighth month, on the day gēngzǐ [31 August 475], Protector-General Chu Yuan was also made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，丙寅，魏徙建昌王長樂為安樂王。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, day bǐngyín: Wei transferred Prince Changle of Jianchang to be Prince of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day bǐngyín [26 December 475], Northern Wei transferred Prince Changle of Jianchang to the title Prince of Anle.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏城陽王長壽卒。

translations.literal: On day jǐchǒu Prince Changshou of Chengyang of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jǐchǒu [10 January 476] Prince Changshou of Chengyang of Northern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史建平王景素，孝友清令，服用儉素，又好文學，禮接士大夫，由是有美譽；

translations.literal: Prince Jingsu of Pingping, governor of South Xuzhou, was filial, friendly, pure, and upright, frugal in dress and fare, fond of literature, courteous to scholar-officials, and thereby enjoyed a fine reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingsu of Pingping, governor of South Xuzhou, was known for filial piety, amiability, and integrity, lived simply, loved literature, and treated scholar-officials with courtesy, winning a fine reputation;

sentences.zh: 太宗特愛之，異其禮秩。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong especially favored him and treated his rank and rites as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong especially favored him and granted him exceptional honors.

sentences.zh: 時太祖諸子俱盡，諸孫唯景素為長；

translations.literal: At the time all the sons of Emperor Taizu were gone, and among the grandsons only Jingsu was eldest;
translations.idiomatic: By then all of Emperor Taizu's sons were dead, and among the grandsons only Jingsu was the eldest;

sentences.zh: 帝凶狂失德，朝野皆屬意於景素。

translations.literal: the emperor was fierce, mad, and devoid of virtue, and court and country alike looked to Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor was violent and debauched, and both court and country looked to Jingsu.

sentences.zh: 帝外家陳氏深惡之，楊運長、阮佃夫等欲專權勢，不利立長君，亦欲除之。

translations.literal: The emperor's maternal clan, the Chen family, deeply hated him; Yang Yunchang, Ruan Tainfu, and others wished to monopolize power and disliked establishing an elder ruler, and also wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's maternal Chen clan hated him deeply; Yang Yunchang, Ruan Tainfu, and others wanted to monopolize power, disliked elevating an elder prince, and also sought to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 其腹心將佐多勸景素舉兵，鎮軍參軍濟陽江淹獨諫之，景素不悅。

translations.literal: His trusted generals and aides mostly urged Jingsu to raise troops; Jiang Yan of Jiyang, Major on the General Who Guards the Army's staff, alone remonstrated, and Jingsu was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: His closest generals and staff mostly urged Jingsu to rebel; only Jiang Yan of Jiyang, an army major, dissented, and Jingsu was displeased.

sentences.zh: 是歲，防閣將軍王季符得罪於景素，單騎亡奔建康，告景素謀反。

translations.literal: That year the garrison general Wang Jifu offended Jingsu, fled alone on horseback to Jiankang, and reported that Jingsu intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That year garrison general Wang Jifu offended Jingsu, fled alone to Jiankang, and accused him of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 運長等即欲發兵討之，袁粲、蕭道成以為不可；

translations.literal: Yunchang and the rest at once wished to send troops to punish him; Yuan Can and Xiao Daocheng thought it could not be done;
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang and his faction at once wanted to send troops against him; Yuan Can and Xiao Daocheng objected;

sentences.zh: 景素亦遣世子延齡詣闕自陳。

translations.literal: Jingsu also sent his heir Yanling to the palace to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu also sent his heir Yanling to court to plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 乃徙季符於梁州，奪景素征北將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jifu was banished to Liangzhou, and Jingsu was stripped of his titles as General Who Conquers the North and Grandee of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu was banished to Liangzhou, and Jingsu was stripped of his titles as General Who Conquers the North and Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
